 ABOUT THIS PROXY STATEMENT/PROSPECTUS 
 This proxy statement/prospectus relates to an Agreement and Plan of Merger and Reorganization, dated as of June&#160;24, 2026 (as amended, modified, supplemented or waived from time to time, the &#8220; Merger Agreement &#8221;), by and among Churchill Capital Corp&#160;XI, a Cayman Islands exempted company (&#8220; CCXI &#8221;), BLB Merger Sub, Inc., a Delaware corporation and a direct, wholly -owned subsidiary of CCXI (&#8220; Merger Sub &#8221;) and Agility Robotics, Inc., a Delaware corporation (&#8220; Agility &#8221;), a copy of which is attached to this proxy statement/prospectus as an annex thereto. 
 The Merger Agreement, among other things and subject to the terms and conditions contained therein, provides for (a)&#160;the transfer of the registration of CCXI by way of continuation from the Cayman Islands to the State of Delaware (the &#8220; Domestication &#8221;), and (b)&#160;following the Domestication, the merger of Merger Sub with and into Agility with Agility continuing as the surviving entity and as a wholly -owned subsidiary of CCXI (the &#8220; Merger ,&#8221; and, together with the Domestication and other transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement and the related agreements, the &#8220; Transactions &#8221; or the &#8220; business combination &#8221;). In connection with the business combination, CCXI will change its name to &#8220;Agility Robotics, Inc.&#8221; We refer to the new public entity following the consummation of the business combination as the &#8220; Post -Closing Company .&#8221; 
 This proxy statement/prospectus serves as: 
 &#8226; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; a proxy statement for the extraordinary general meeting of CCXI, where CCXI shareholders will vote on, among other things, proposals to (1)&#160;approve the Merger Agreement and the business combination (the &#8220; business combination proposal &#8221;), (2)&#160;approve the Domestication on a non -binding advisory basis (the &#8220; domestication proposal &#8221;), (3)&#160;approve and adopt, with effect from the Domestication, the amended and restated certificate of incorporation (&#8220; Proposed Certificate of Incorporation &#8221;) and bylaws (&#8220; Proposed Bylaws &#8221;) of the Post -Closing Company on a non -binding advisory basis (the &#8220; organizational documents proposal &#8221;), (4)&#160;approve, on a non -binding advisory basis, certain of the material differences between CCXI&#8217;s current Amended and Restated Memorandum and Articles of Association (the &#8220; CCXI current articles of association &#8221;) and the Proposed Certificate of Incorporation and the Proposed Bylaws (the &#8220; advisory organizational documents proposal &#8221;), (5)&#160;approve the issuance of shares of common stock of the Post -Closing Company following the Domestication in connection with the Merger (the &#8220; stock issuance proposal &#8221;), (6)&#160;approve and adopt the Incentive Plan and the material terms thereof, including the authorization of the initial share reserve thereunder (the &#8220; incentive plan proposal &#8221;), (7)&#160;approve and adopt the ESPP and the material terms thereof, including the authorization of the initial share reserve thereunder (the &#8220; ESPP proposal &#8221;), (8)&#160;approve, on a non -binding advisory basis, the election of directors to serve staggered terms on the Post -Closing Company Board following the consummation of the business combination until immediately following the date of the 2027, 2028 and 2029 annual stockholder meetings, or in each case until their respective successors are duly elected and qualified, or until their earlier resignation, removal or death (the &#8220; director election proposal &#8221;) and (9)&#160;approve the adjournment of the extraordinary general meeting to a later date or dates, if necessary, to permit further solicitation and vote of proxies in the event that there are insufficient votes for the approval of one or more of the proposals at the extraordinary general meeting (&#8220; adjournment proposal &#8221;); and 
 &#8226; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; a prospectus for the shares of common stock of the Post -Closing Company that CCXI securityholders and Agility securityholders will receive as consideration in the business combination.

 PRELIMINARY&#160;&#8212;&#160;SUBJECT TO COMPLETION, DATED September 4, 2026 
 PROXY STATEMENT FOR EXTRAORDINARY GENERAL MEETING IN LIEU OF AN ANNUAL MEETING OF 
 Churchill Capital Corp&#160;XI

 PROSPECTUS FOR UP TO &#160;&#160;&#160; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; SHARES OF COMMON STOCK 
 OF 
 CHURCHILL CAPITAL CORP&#160;XI 
 (TO BE RENAMED &#8220;AGILITY ROBOTICS, INC.&#8221; FOLLOWING DOMESTICATION IN THE STATE OF DELAWARE AND IN CONNECTION WITH THE BUSINESS COMBINATION DESCRIBED IN THIS PROXY STATEMENT) 
 ____________________ 
 The board of directors of Churchill Capital Corp&#160;XI, a Cayman Islands exempted company (&#8220; CCXI ,&#8221; &#8220; we &#8221; or &#8220; our &#8221;), has approved the Agreement and Plan of Merger and Reorganization, dated as of June&#160;24, 2026 (as amended, modified, supplemented or waived from time to time, the &#8220; Merger Agreement &#8221;), by and among CCXI, BLB Merger Sub, Inc., a Delaware corporation and a direct, wholly -owned subsidiary of CCXI (&#8220; Merger Sub &#8221;) and Agility Robotics, Inc., a Delaware corporation (&#8220; Agility &#8221;). The Merger Agreement, among other things and subject to the terms and conditions contained therein, provides for (a)&#160;the transfer of the registration of CCXI by way of continuation from the Cayman Islands to the State of Delaware (the &#8220; Domestication &#8221;), and (b)&#160;following the Domestication, the merger of Merger Sub with and into Agility, with Agility continuing as the surviving entity and as a wholly -owned subsidiary of CCXI (collectively, the &#8220; Merger ,&#8221; and, together with the Domestication and other transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement and the related agreements, the &#8220; Transactions &#8221; or the &#8220; business combination &#8221;). In connection with the business combination, CCXI will change its name to &#8220;Agility Robotics, Inc.&#8221; We refer to the new public entity following the consummation of the business combination as the &#8220; Post -Closing Company .&#8221; Subject to the terms and conditions of the Merger Agreement, the value of the aggregate consideration to be paid to Agility stockholders, holders of Agility options and Agility convertible securities will be $2,500,000,000 (the &#8220; Equity Value &#8221;), which consideration will be paid entirely in shares of common stock, par value $0.0001 per share, of the Post -Closing Company (&#8220; Post -Closing Company common stock &#8221;), valued in an amount equal to the CCXI shareholder redemption per share price (as defined herein). At the Effective Time, each share of Agility common stock issued and outstanding immediately prior to the Effective Time (other than Excluded Shares and Dissenting Shares) will be automatically cancelled and converted into the right to receive a number of shares of Post -Closing Company common stock equal to the Exchange Ratio. The Exchange Ratio is based on the per share Equity Value (calculated in accordance with the Merger Agreement). Subject to the assumptions described herein, as of the date of this proxy statement/prospectus, we estimate that the Exchange Ratio will be approximately&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;shares of Post -Closing Company common stock for each issued and outstanding share of Agility common stock (after giving effect to the conversions of Agility preferred stock, Agility SAFEs and all equity securities issued or issuable in connection with a Permitted Bridge Financing (as defined herein), into Agility common stock); see the section entitled &#8220; Proposal&#160;No.&#160;1 &#8212;&#160;The Business Combination Proposal&#160;&#8212;&#160;General&#160;&#8212;&#160;Structure of the Transactions .&#8221; 
 Accordingly, this proxy statement/prospectus covers up to an aggregate of &#160;&#160;&#160; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; shares of Post -Closing Company common stock, representing the estimated maximum number of shares to be issued to the existing securityholders of Agility at the Closing. 
 To raise additional proceeds to fund the Transactions, CCXI has entered into subscription agreements (&#8220; PIPE Subscription Agreements &#8221;) with certain investment funds (the &#8220; PIPE Investors &#8221;), pursuant to which, subject to the terms and conditions thereof, CCXI has agreed to issue and sell to the PIPE Investors, and the PIPE Investors have agreed to purchase an aggregate of, $201,025,000 of CCXI common stock at a purchase price of $10.00 per share, which we refer to as the &#8220; PIPE Investment .&#8221; The PIPE Subscription Agreements contain customary representations, warranties, covenants and agreements of CCXI and the PIPE Investors and are subject to customary closing conditions and termination rights.

 Interests of Sponsor and its Affiliates 
 In June&#160;2025, Churchill Sponsor&#160;XI LLC (the &#8220; Sponsor &#8221;) acquired an aggregate of 8,625,000 CCXI Founder Shares (as defined herein), for approximately $0.002 per share. In November&#160;2025, CCXI, through a share capitalization, issued the Sponsor an additional 2,875,000 CCXI Founder Shares. In December&#160;2025, CCXI, through a share capitalization, issued the Sponsor an additional 2,300,000 CCXI Founder Shares, for which the Sponsor now holds 13,800,000 CCXI Founder Shares in the aggregate. The CCXI Founder Shares (including the Class&#160;A ordinary shares of CCXI, par value $0.0001 per share (the &#8220; CCXI Class&#160;A Ordinary Shares &#8221;) issuable upon exercise thereof) may not, subject to certain limited exceptions, be transferred, assigned or sold by the holder. See the section entitled &#8220; Certain Relationships and Related Person Transactions&#160;&#8212;&#160;CCXI Related Person Transactions .&#8221; 
 In December&#160;2025, the Sponsor purchased an aggregate of 500,000 CCXI private placement units (as defined herein), at a price of $10.00 per unit, for an aggregate purchase price of $5,000,000, in the private placement in connection with the CCXI IPO (as defined herein). Each CCXI private placement warrant contained in the CCXI private placement units is exercisable to purchase one whole CCXI Class&#160;A Ordinary Share at a price of $11.50&#160;per share. The CCXI private placement warrants will become exercisable 30&#160;days after the completion of the business combination. The CCXI private placement warrants (including the CCXI Class&#160;A Ordinary Shares issuable upon exercise thereof) may not, subject to certain limited exceptions, be transferred, assigned or sold by the holder until 30&#160;days after the completion of the business combination; however, if the business combination is consummated, each Sponsor Signatory (as defined below) holding the CCXI private placement warrants has agreed to the Sponsor Lockup (as defined herein). See the section entitled &#8220; Proposal&#160;No.&#160;1 &#8212;&#160;The Business Combination Proposal&#160;&#8212;&#160;Certain Agreements Related to the Business Combination&#160;&#8212;&#160;Sponsor Agreement. &#8221; The CCXI private placement warrants are non -redeemable and exercisable for cash or on a &#8220;cashless basis.&#8221; The CCXI private placement warrants do not expire except upon liquidation. 
 In December&#160;2025, CCXI agreed to reimburse M.&#160;Klein Associates, Inc., the managing member of the Sponsor, through its affiliate The Klein Group, LLC, an amount equal to $30,000 per month for office space, utilities and secretarial and administrative support made available to us. In addition, CCXI has agreed, pursuant to an administrative services and indemnification agreement with the managing member of the Sponsor, that it will indemnify the Sponsor from any claims arising out of or relating to the CCXI IPO, or its operations or conduct of its business (including the business combination) or any claims against CCXI alleging any expressed or implied management or endorsement by them of any of its activities or any express or implied association between the Sponsor and CCXI, which agreement provides that the indemnified parties cannot access the funds held in CCXI&#8217;s trust account. Upon completion of the business combination or CCXI&#8217;s liquidation, the obligation to continue paying these monthly fees will be terminated and CCXI will cease paying these monthly fees. 
 Michael Klein, a director of CCXI, and the controlling shareholder of M.&#160;Klein Associates, Inc., which is the managing member of the Sponsor, may be deemed to beneficially own the securities of CCXI owned by Sponsor. For more information about our officers&#8217; and directors&#8217; economic interests in the Transactions, see the section entitled &#8220; Beneficial Ownership of Securities .&#8221; 
 Prior to or in connection with the completion of the business combination, there may be payment by CCXI to the Sponsor, its officers or directors, or CCXI&#8217;s or their affiliates, of a finder&#8217;s fee, advisory fee, consulting fee or success fee for any services they render in order to effectuate the completion of the business combination, which, if made prior to the completion of the initial business combination, will be paid from (1)&#160;funds held outside the trust account or (2)&#160;permitted withdrawals (as defined herein). 
 The Sponsor, its executive officers and directors, or any of their respective affiliates, are entitled to reimbursement for any out -of-pocket expenses incurred in connection with activities on CCXI&#8217;s behalf such as identifying potential target businesses and performing due diligence on suitable business combinations. CCXI&#8217;s audit committee reviews on a quarterly basis all payments that were made to the Sponsor, its officers or directors or CCXI&#8217;s or their affiliates. Any such payments prior to an initial business combination are made from funds held outside the trust account, including permitted withdrawals. 
 Subject to the terms of the Merger Agreement, there is no cap or ceiling on the reimbursement of out -of-pocket expenses incurred by such persons in connection with activities on CCXI&#8217;s behalf.

 In June&#160;2025, CCXI and the Sponsor entered into a loan agreement, whereby the Sponsor agreed to loan CCXI an aggregate of up to $600,000 to cover expenses related to the CCXI IPO, pursuant to the IPO Promissory Note (as defined herein). This loan was non -interest bearing and payable on the earlier of December&#160;31, 2026, or the date on which the Company consummated the CCXI IPO.&#160;As of June 30, 2026 and December&#160;31, 2025, there was $0 outstanding under the IPO Promissory Note. The Company repaid the borrowings in full at the closing of the CCXI IPO.&#160;Borrowings under the IPO Promissory Note are no longer available. 
 In addition, in order to fund working capital deficiencies or finance transaction costs in connection with an intended business combination, the Sponsor, CCXI or their respective affiliates may, but are not obligated to, loan CCXI funds as may be required (the &#8220; Working Capital Loans &#8221;). If CCXI completes the business combination, CCXI would repay the Working Capital Loans. In the event that the business combination does not close, CCXI may use a portion of the working capital held outside the trust account to repay the Working Capital Loans but no proceeds from the trust account would be used for such repayment. Initially, up to $1,500,000 of such Working Capital Loans may be converted into units of the Post -Closing Company at a price of $10.00 per unit, at the option of the lender. On August 7, 2026, in connection with the issuance of the August 2026 Note (as defined below), the CCXI Board approved an additional $1,500,000 of Working Capital Loans that may be convertible into units of the Post -Closing Company at a price of $10.00 per unit at the option of the lender. The units and their underlying securities would be identical to the CCXI private placement units. Except as set forth above, the terms of the Working Capital Loans by CCXI&#8217;s officers and directors, if any, have not been determined and no written agreements exist with respect to the Working Capital Loans. Prior to the completion of the business combination, CCXI does not expect to seek loans from parties other than the Sponsor or an affiliate of the Sponsor as CCXI does not believe third parties will be willing to loan such funds and provide a waiver against any and all rights to seek access to funds in the trust account. As of June 30, 2026 and December&#160;31, 2025, CCXI had no borrowings under the Working Capital Loans. On July&#160;2, 2026, CCXI issued an unsecured promissory note in the aggregate principal amount of up to $1,500,000 to the Sponsor (the &#8220; July 2026 Note &#8221;), for working capital needs. As of the date of this proxy statement/prospectus, CCXI has borrowed the full $1,500,000 available under the July 2026 Note. On August 7, 2026, CCXI issued an additional unsecured promissory note in the aggregate principal amount of up to $1,500,000 (the &#8220; August 2026 Note &#8221;), for working capital needs. The August 2026 Note may be convertible into units of the Post -Closing Company at a price of $10.00 per unit at the option of the lender. As of the date of this proxy statement/prospectus, CCXI has borrowed $750,000 under the August 2026 Note. Both the July 2026 Note and August 2026 Note mature upon the earlier of the closing of CCXI&#8217;s initial business combination or CCXI&#8217;s liquidation. 
 The retention of 13,800,000 Founder Shares and 500,000 CCXI Private Placement Units by Sponsor and the units of the Post -Closing Company issuable to the Sponsor upon the conversion of $3,000,000 of the Working Capital Loans at $10.00 per unit at Closing may result in a material dilution of the equity interests of non -redeeming CCXI public shareholders. See &#8220; Questions and Answers &#8212; What equity stake will current CCXI shareholders and Agility stockholders hold in the Post -Closing Company immediately after the consummation of the business combination?&#8221; and &#8220; Dilution &#8221; for further information. 
 CCXI has agreed to indemnify the Sponsor and its members (present and former), managers and affiliates and their respective present and former officers and directors to the fullest extent permitted under applicable law from any claims made by CCXI or a third party in respect of any investment opportunities sourced by them or any liability arising with respect to their activities in connection with CCXI&#8217;s affairs, to the extent that such indemnification, hold harmless and exoneration obligations with respect to such matters are not expressly covered by a separate written agreement between CCXI and any such party. Such indemnity will provide that the indemnified parties cannot access the funds held in the trust account. 
 After the business combination, members of CCXI&#8217;s management team who remain with CCXI may be paid consulting, management or other fees from the combined company with any and all amounts being fully disclosed to CCXI&#8217;s shareholders, to the extent then known, in this proxy statement/prospectus or other proxy solicitation materials (as applicable) furnished to CCXI&#8217;s shareholders. It is unlikely the amount of such compensation is fully known at the time of distribution of this proxy statement/prospectus, or will be fully known at the time of a general meeting held to consider the business combination, as it will be up to the directors of the Post -Closing Company to determine executive and director compensation. 
 Concurrently with the execution of the Merger Agreement, CCXI entered into the Sponsor Agreement (as defined herein) with the Sponsor and the Insiders, which amended and restated that certain letter agreement, dated December&#160;16, 2025, from each of the persons undersigned thereto (the &#8220; Initial Insiders &#8221;).  CCXI&#8217;s articles of association provide that CCXI must complete its initial business combination by the end of the completion window. If CCXI is unable to complete the business combination or another initial business combination by the end of the completion window, CCXI will, as promptly as reasonably possible but not more than ten&#160;business days thereafter, redeem 100% of the outstanding CCXI public shares, at a per share price, payable in cash, equal to the aggregate amount then held in the trust account, including interest earned (which interest shall be net of permitted withdrawals and up to $100,000 of interest to pay dissolution expenses and net of taxes payable) divided by the number of outstanding CCXI public shares, which redemption will completely extinguish CCXI public shareholders&#8217; rights as shareholders (including the right to receive further liquidating distributions, if any), CCXI&#8217;s obligations under Cayman Islands law to provide for claims of creditors and other requirements of applicable law. The Sponsor, directors and officers have entered into a letter agreement with us, pursuant to which, they have waived their rights to liquidating distributions from the trust account with respect to any CCXI Founder Shares held by them if we fail to complete our initial business combination within the completion window. 
 The CCXI public units, CCXI public shares and CCXI public warrants are each traded on the Nasdaq Stock Market (&#8220; Nasdaq &#8221;) under the symbols CCXIU, CCXI and CCXIW, respectively. In connection with the Transactions, CCXI intends to apply to have Post -Closing Company common stock listed on Nasdaq under the symbol &#8220;AGLT,&#8221; and the Post -Closing Company will change its name to &#8220;Agility Robotics, Inc.&#8221; It is a condition to the consummation of the business combination that the shares of Post -Closing Company common stock to be issued (or reserved for issuance) in the Transactions have been listed on Nasdaq or any other stock exchange mutually agreed upon by CCXI and Agility and shall be eligible for continued listing immediately following the closing, but there can be no assurance that such listing condition will be met. If such listing condition is not met, the business combination will not be consummated unless the listing condition is waived by the parties to the Merger Agreement.

 Pursuant to the CCXI current articles of association, a holder of CCXI Class&#160;A Ordinary Shares sold in CCXI&#8217;s initial public offering (whether they were purchased in CCXI&#8217;s initial public offering or thereafter in the open market) (&#8220; CCXI public shares &#8221;) may demand that CCXI redeem such shares for cash if the business combination is consummated (&#8220; redemption rights &#8221;). Eligible holders of CCXI public shares will be entitled to receive cash for these shares only if they demand that CCXI redeem their CCXI public shares for cash no later than the second business&#160;day prior to the initially scheduled vote on the business combination proposal or such later date as our directors may determine (the &#8220; Redemption Deadline &#8221;) by delivering their shares and requesting in writing that CCXI redeem such CCXI public shares for cash to Continental Stock Transfer&#160;&amp; Trust Company, CCXI&#8217;s transfer agent. If an eligible holder of CCXI public shares properly exercises its redemption rights and the business combination is consummated, CCXI will redeem such shares for cash in an amount equal to their pro rata portion of the funds in the trust account holding the proceeds from CCXI&#8217;s initial public offering (the &#8220; trust account &#8221;), calculated as of two&#160;business days prior to the consummation of the business combination and net of certain permitted withdrawals. 
 Notwithstanding the foregoing, a holder of CCXI public shares, together with any affiliate of such holder or any other person with whom such holder is acting in concert or as a &#8220;group&#8221; (as defined in Section&#160;13(d)(3)&#160;of the Exchange&#160;Act), will be restricted from seeking redemption with respect to more than 15% of the CCXI public shares. Accordingly, all CCXI public shares in excess of 15% held by a CCXI public shareholder, together with any affiliate of such holder or any other person with whom such holder is acting in concert or as a &#8220;group,&#8221; will not be redeemed without the prior consent of our directors.  TO EXERCISE YOUR REDEMPTION RIGHTS, YOU MUST ELECT TO HAVE CCXI REDEEM YOUR CCXI PUBLIC SHARES FOR A PRO RATA PORTION OF THE FUNDS HELD IN THE TRUST ACCOUNT (NET OF CERTAIN PERMITTED WITHDRAWALS) AND TENDER SUCH SHARES TO CCXI&#8217;S TRANSFER AGENT AT LEAST TWO BUSINESS DAYS PRIOR TO THE INITIALLY SCHEDULED VOTE AT THE EXTRAORDINARY GENERAL MEETING. &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; YOU MAY TENDER YOUR CCXI PUBLIC SHARES BY EITHER DELIVERING YOUR SHARE CERTIFICATE TO THE TRANSFER AGENT OR BY DELIVERING SUCH SHARES ELECTRONICALLY USING THE DEPOSITORY TRUST COMPANY&#8217;S DWAC (DEPOSIT AND WITHDRAWAL AT CUSTODIAN) SYSTEM.&#160;IF THE BUSINESS COMBINATION IS NOT COMPLETED, THEN SUCH CCXI PUBLIC SHARES WILL NOT BE REDEEMED FOR CASH.&#160;IF YOU HOLD CCXI PUBLIC SHARES IN STREET NAME, YOU WILL NEED TO INSTRUCT THE ACCOUNT EXECUTIVE AT YOUR BANK OR BROKER TO WITHDRAW SUCH SHARES FROM YOUR ACCOUNT IN ORDER TO EXERCISE YOUR REDEMPTION RIGHTS.&#160;PLEASE SEE THE SECTION ENTITLED &#8220; EXTRAORDINARY GENERAL MEETING OF CCXI&#160;&#8212;&#160;REDEMPTION RIGHTS &#8221; FOR MORE SPECIFIC INSTRUCTIONS. 
 Immediately following the Redemption Deadline, a public shareholder that makes an election to redeem its CCXI public shares (an &#8220; Election &#8221;) may withdraw its Election with respect to all or a portion of its CCXI public shares for which it previously submitted an Election (an &#8220; Election Reversal &#8221;). 
 TO MAKE AN ELECTION REVERSAL WITH RESPECT TO YOUR CCXI PUBLIC SHARES, YOU MUST SUBMIT A WRITTEN REQUEST TO THE TRANSFER AGENT, AFTER 5:00 P.M.&#160;EASTERN TIME ON &#160;&#160;&#160; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; , 2026, THE DATE THAT IS TWO BUSINESS DAYS PRIOR TO THE SCHEDULED VOTE AT THE EXTRAORDINARY GENERAL MEETING, AND PRIOR TO THE SCHEDULED VOTE AT THE EXTRAORDINARY GENERAL MEETING, THAT THE ELECTION TO REDEEM YOUR CCXI PUBLIC SHARES BE REVERSED, INCLUDING THE LEGAL NAME, PHONE NUMBER, AND ADDRESS OF THE BENEFICIAL OWNER OF THE SHARES FOR WHICH REVERSAL IS REQUESTED AND THE NUMBER OR PERCENTAGE OF SHARES FOR WHICH REVERSAL IS REQUESTED.&#160;IF YOU HOLD THE SHARES IN STREET NAME, YOU WILL NEED TO INSTRUCT THE ACCOUNT EXECUTIVE AT YOUR BANK OR BROKER TO REQUEST REVERSAL OF THE ELECTION TO REDEEM AT THE TRANSFER AGENT.

Only CCXI shareholders of record at the close of business on &#160;&#160;&#160; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; , 2026 are entitled to notice of the extraordinary general meeting and to vote and have their votes counted at the extraordinary general meeting and any adjournments or postponements thereof. 
 After careful consideration, the CCXI Board has unanimously determined that the business combination proposal, domestication proposal, organizational documents proposal, advisory organizational documents proposal, stock issuance proposal, incentive plan proposal, ESPP proposal, director election proposal and, if necessary, the adjournment proposal are fair to, and in the best interests of, CCXI and its shareholders and unanimously recommends that you vote or give instruction to vote &#8220;FOR&#8221; the business combination proposal, &#8220;FOR&#8221; the domestication proposal, &#8220;FOR&#8221; the organizational documents proposal, &#8220;FOR&#8221; the advisory organizational documents proposal, &#8220;FOR&#8221; the stock issuance proposal, &#8220;FOR&#8221; the incentive plan proposal, &#8220;FOR&#8221; the ESPP proposal, &#8220;FOR&#8221; each of the director nominees named in the director election proposal and, if presented, &#8220;FOR&#8221; the adjournment proposal. When you consider the CCXI Board&#8217;s recommendation of these proposals, you should keep in mind that our directors and officers, as well as Churchill Sponsor&#160;XI LLC, our sponsor (the &#8220; Sponsor &#8221;), have interests in the Transactions that are different from, or in addition to, the interests of CCXI shareholders generally. Please see the section entitled &#8220; Proposal&#160;No.&#160;1 &#8212;&#160;The Business Combination Proposal&#160;&#8212;&#160;Interests of Certain CCXI Persons in the Business Combination &#8221; for additional information. The CCXI Board was aware of and considered these interests, among other matters, including the fairness opinion of Ocean Tomo, in evaluating and negotiating the Transactions and in recommending to CCXI shareholders that they vote in favor of the proposals presented at the extraordinary general meeting. 
 Consummation of the business combination is conditioned on the approval of each of the other condition precedent proposals. If any of those proposals are not approved at the extraordinary general meeting (or any adjournment or postponement thereof), then unless certain conditions in the Merger Agreement are waived by the applicable parties to the Merger Agreement, the Merger Agreement may be terminated and the business combination may not be consummated. 
 Pursuant to the CCXI current articles of association, a holder of CCXI Class&#160;A Ordinary Shares sold in CCXI&#8217;s initial public offering (whether they were purchased in CCXI&#8217;s initial public offering or thereafter in the open market) (&#8220; CCXI public shares &#8221;) may demand that CCXI redeem such shares for cash if the business combination is consummated (&#8220; redemption rights &#8221;). Such redemption rights are not available to our Sponsor, officers or directors. Eligible holders of CCXI public shares will be entitled to receive cash for these shares only if they demand that CCXI redeem their CCXI public shares for cash no later than the second business&#160;day prior to the initially scheduled vote on the business combination proposal or such later date as our directors may determine (the &#8220; Redemption Deadline &#8221;) by delivering their shares and requesting in writing that CCXI redeem such CCXI public shares for cash to Continental Stock Transfer&#160;&amp; Trust Company, CCXI&#8217;s transfer agent. If the business combination is not completed, the CCXI public shares will not be redeemed. If an eligible holder of CCXI public shares properly exercises their redemption rights and the business combination is consummated, CCXI will redeem such shares for cash in an amount equal to their pro rata portion of the funds in the trust account holding the proceeds from CCXI&#8217;s initial public offering (the &#8220; trust account &#8221;), calculated as of two&#160;business days prior to the consummation of the business combination and net of certain permitted withdrawals. 
 Notwithstanding the foregoing, a holder of CCXI public shares, together with any affiliate of such holder or any other person with whom such holder is acting in concert or as a &#8220;group&#8221; (as defined in Section&#160;13(d)(3)&#160;of the Exchange&#160;Act), will be restricted from seeking redemption with respect to more than 15% of the CCXI public shares. Accordingly, all CCXI public shares in excess of 15% held by a CCXI public shareholder, together with any affiliate of such holder or any other person with whom such holder is acting in concert or as a &#8220;group,&#8221; will not be redeemed without the prior consent of our directors. Such redemption rights are also not available to our Sponsor, officers or directors.

 &#8226; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Churchill Capital Corp&#160;XI, a Cayman Islands exempted company (&#8220; CCXI ,&#8221; &#8220; we ,&#8221; &#8220; us ,&#8221; or &#8220; our &#8221;), is a special purpose acquisition company formed for the purpose of effecting a merger, amalgamation, share exchange, asset acquisition, share purchase, reorganization or similar business combination with one or more businesses. 
 &#8226; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; On December &#160; 18, 2025, CCXI consummated its initial public offering (the &#8220; CCXI IPO &#8221;) of 41,400,000&#160;units (&#8220; CCXI public units &#8221;), including 5,400,000 CCXI public units under the underwriters&#8217; over -allotment option. Each CCXI public unit consists of one Class&#160;A ordinary share of CCXI, par value $0.0001 per share (the &#8220; CCXI Class&#160;A Ordinary Shares &#8221;), and one -tenth of one redeemable warrant of CCXI (each, a &#8220; CCXI public warrant &#8221;), with each whole CCXI public warrant entitling the holder thereof to purchase one Class&#160;A Ordinary Share for $11.50 per share. The CCXI public units were sold at an offering price of $10.00 per unit, generating gross proceeds to CCXI of $414,000,000. Simultaneously with the consummation of the CCXI IPO and the exercise of the underwriters&#8217; over -allotment option, CCXI consummated the private placement of 500,000&#160;units (the &#8220; CCXI private placement units &#8221;) to the Sponsor at a price of $10.00 per unit, generating total proceeds of $5,000,000. Transaction costs amounted to $19,618,232, consisting of $3,000,000 of underwriting fees, $15,990,000 of deferred underwriting fees (of which $1,500,000 has been paid and $14,490,000 remains deferred) and $628,232 of other offering costs. 
 &#8226; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Following the consummation of the CCXI IPO, $414,000,000 was deposited into a U.S. -based trust account with Continental Stock Transfer&#160;&amp; Trust Company acting as trustee. Except as described in the prospectus for the CCXI IPO, these proceeds will not be released until the earlier of the completion of an initial business combination and CCXI&#8217;s redemption of 100% of the outstanding CCXI public shares upon its failure to consummate an initial business combination within the completion window. 
 &#8226; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Agility Robotics, Inc., a Delaware corporation (&#8220; Agility &#8221;), is a leading humanoid robotics and physical AI company focused on delivering fully autonomous humanoid robots that will improve the future of labor. See the sections entitled &#8220; Information About Agility ,&#8221; &#8220; Agility&#8217;s Management&#8217;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations &#8221; and &#8220; Board of Directors and Management After the Business Combination .&#8221; 
 &#8226; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; On June &#160; 24, 2026, CCXI entered into the Merger Agreement, which, among other things and subject to the terms and conditions contained therein, provides for the merger of Merger Sub with and into Agility, with Agility continuing as the surviving entity and as a wholly -owned subsidiary of CCXI (the &#8220; Merger &#8221; and, together with the Domestication and other transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement and the related agreements, the &#8220; Transactions &#8221; or the &#8220; business combination &#8221;). 
 &#8226; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Subject to the terms and conditions of the Merger Agreement, the value of the aggregate consideration to be paid to Agility stockholders, holders of Agility options and Agility convertible securities will be $2,500,000,000 (the &#8220; Equity Value &#8221;), which consideration will be paid entirely in shares of common stock, par value $0.0001 per share, of the Post -Closing Company (&#8220; Post -Closing Company common stock &#8221;), valued in an amount equal to the CCXI shareholder redemption per share price (as defined herein). At the Effective Time, each share of Agility common stock issued and outstanding immediately prior to the Effective Time (other than Excluded Shares and Dissenting Shares) will be automatically cancelled and converted into the right to receive a number of shares of Post -Closing Company common stock equal to the Exchange Ratio. The Exchange Ratio is based on the per share Equity Value (calculated in accordance with the Merger Agreement). If any of those proposals are not approved&#160;at the extraordinary general meeting (or any adjournment or postponement thereof), then unless certain conditions in the Merger Agreement are waived by the applicable parties to the Merger Agreement, the Merger Agreement may be terminated and the business combination may not be consummated. 
 The vote of CCXI shareholders is important. CCXI shareholders are encouraged to vote as soon as possible after carefully reviewing this proxy statement/prospectus. 
 Q. &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Why is CCXI proposing the business combination? 
 A. &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; CCXI was organized to effect a merger, amalgamation, share exchange, asset acquisition, share purchase, reorganization or similar business combination with one or more businesses. 
 

 xvi 
 Table of Contents 

 
 On December&#160;18, 2025, CCXI completed its initial public offering (the &#8220; CCXI IPO &#8221;) of CCXI public units at an offering price of $10.00 per unit, each consisting of one share of CCXI Class&#160;A Ordinary Shares and one tenth of one warrant, raising total gross proceeds of approximately $414,000,000. Simultaneously with the closing of the CCXI IPO and pursuant to a private placement of the CCXI private placement units at a price of $10.00 per unit (the &#8220; CCXI Private Placement &#8221;), CCXI raised total gross proceeds of approximately $5,000,000. Since the CCXI IPO and the CCXI Private Placement, CCXI&#8217;s activity has been limited to the evaluation of initial business combination candidates. 
 Agility was founded in 2015. 
 Agility is a commercial humanoid company. Agility&#8217;s mission is to build robot partners that augment the human workforce, ultimately enabling humans to be more human. Its flagship humanoid robot, Digit, is a multi -purpose , human -centric robot Made for Work&#8482; and currently operating in manufacturing, distribution, and logistics environments to fill physical labor shortages. Through more than a decade of advancing robotics into real -world commercial deployment, Agility has established itself as one of the only humanoid companies with multiple&#160;years of operational experience in real customer environments. 
 The CCXI Board conducted extensive due diligence on Agility&#8217;s business, financial condition, management team, and future growth prospects in executing upon and achieving its business plan. The CCXI Board considered the results of the diligence review, including the deep technical expertise of Agility&#8217;s founders and engineering leadership in humanoid robotics and physical AI, the commercial leadership team&#8217;s experience scaling enterprise technology businesses, Agility&#8217;s commercial progress and customer deployments, the large expected market opportunity for collaboratively safe humanoid robots, including Digit, designed to address persistent labor shortages across warehouse, manufacturing, logistics and other industrial environments, Agility&#8217;s proprietary technology platform and manufacturing capabilities, and Agility&#8217;s strategic relationships with leading customers and technology partners. As a result, CCXI believes that the business combination will provide CCXI shareholders with an opportunity to participate in the ownership of a company with growth potential. Please see the section entitled &#8220; Proposal&#160;No.&#160;1 &#8212;&#160;The Business Combination Proposal&#160;&#8212;&#160;Reasons for Approval of the Transactions. &#8221; 
 Q. &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Why is CCXI providing shareholders with the opportunity to vote on the business combination? 
 A. &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Under the CCXI current articles of association, CCXI must provide all holders of CCXI public shares with the opportunity to have their CCXI public shares redeemed upon the consummation of an initial business combination either in conjunction with a tender offer or in conjunction with a shareholder vote. For business and other reasons, CCXI has elected to provide its shareholders with the opportunity to have their CCXI public shares redeemed in connection with a shareholder vote rather than a tender offer. Therefore, CCXI is seeking to obtain the approval of its shareholders of the business combination proposal in order to allow CCXI public shareholders to exercise their redemption rights in connection with the Closing. 
 Q. &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; What will happen in the business combination? 
 A. &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Pursuant to the Merger Agreement and the related agreements, and upon the terms and subject to the conditions set forth therein, CCXI will acquire Agility and Agility will become a publicly traded company through the business combination. The business combination consists of (1)&#160;the transfer of the registration of CCXI by way of continuation from the Cayman Islands to the State of Delaware (the &#8220; Domestication &#8221;), and (2)&#160;following the Domestication, the merger of Merger Sub with and into Agility, with Agility continuing as the surviving entity and as a wholly -owned subsidiary of CCXI.&#160;Subject to the assumptions described herein, as of the date of this proxy statement/prospectus, at the Closing, we estimate that approximately &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; shares of Post -Closing Company common stock will be issued to holders of Agility common stock in the Merger, in exchange for all outstanding shares of Agility common stock (including shares of Agility common stock resulting from the conversions of Agility preferred stock, Agility SAFEs and all equity securities issued or issuable in connection with a Permitted Bridge Financing, immediately prior to the Closing). We also estimate that we will reserve for issuance up to &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; shares of Post -Closing Company common stock in respect of the Agility options pursuant to the terms of the Merger Agreement. The reserved shares referred to in the immediately preceding sentence are not included in the&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;shares the sale and issuance of which are registered by this registration statement, and are not subject to registration rights, but will be registered in a registration statement on Form&#160;S -8 to the extent that such Agility options were granted to or acquired by service providers of Agility in accordance with the Agility Stock Plans. See the section entitled &#8220; Proposal&#160;No.&#160;1 &#8212;&#160;The Business Combination Proposal&#160;&#8212;&#160;General&#160;&#8212;&#160;Merger Consideration. &#8221;

 Q. &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Following the business combination, will CCXI&#8217;s securities continue to trade on a stock exchange?

 Q. &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Why is CCXI proposing the Domestication? 
 A. &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; The Domestication is part of the business combination. The CCXI Board believes that there are significant advantages to Agility that will arise as a result of a change of CCXI&#8217;s domicile to the State of Delaware, including: (1)&#160;the prominence, predictability and flexibility of the DGCL; (2)&#160;Delaware&#8217;s well -established principles of corporate governance; and (3)&#160;the increased ability for Delaware corporations to attract and retain qualified directors. Further, the CCXI Board believes that any direct benefit that the DGCL provides to a corporation also indirectly benefits its shareholders, who are the owners of the corporation. Each of the foregoing are discussed in greater detail in the section of this proxy statement/prospectus entitled &#8220; Proposal&#160;No.&#160;2 &#8212;&#160;The Domestication Proposal&#160;&#8212;&#160;Reasons for the Domestication .&#8221; 
 Under CCXI current articles of association, CCXI&#8217;s directors have the authority to resolve that CCXI be registered by way of continuation in a jurisdiction outside the Cayman Islands or such other jurisdiction in which it is for the time being incorporated, registered or existing (including, but not limited to, the approval of the organizational documents to be adopted by the Company in such other jurisdiction to the extent applicable). Accordingly, it is not necessary for CCXI to receive shareholder consent to the Domestication, and the domestication proposal and the organizational documents proposal are therefore being presented to CCXI shareholders on a non -binding advisory basis only. 
 To effect the Domestication, CCXI will file an application to deregister with the Cayman Islands Registrar of Companies, together with the necessary accompanying documents and fees, and file the Proposed Certificate of Incorporation and a certificate of corporate domestication with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware, under which CCXI will be domesticated and continue as a Delaware corporation. 
 The approval of the domestication proposal is a condition to closing the business combination under the Merger Agreement. The approval of the domestication proposal requires a special resolution, being the affirmative vote of holders of at least two -thirds of the CCXI Ordinary Shares represented at the extraordinary general meeting by attendance via the virtual meeting website, in person or by proxy, and entitled to vote at the extraordinary general meeting, voting together as a single class. Abstentions and broker non -votes , while considered present for the purposes of establishing a quorum, will not count as votes cast at the extraordinary general meeting.

 Q. &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; How will the Domestication affect my CCXI Class&#160;A Ordinary Shares and CCXI Warrants? 
 A. &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; In connection with, and upon the effectiveness of, the Domestication: (1)&#160;each CCXI Class&#160;A Ordinary Share issued and outstanding immediately prior to the Domestication will remain outstanding and will automatically convert, on a one -for-one basis, into one share of CCXI common stock; and (2)&#160;each of the issued and outstanding CCXI Warrants will automatically convert into warrants (&#8220; CCXI Delaware Warrants &#8221;) to acquire a corresponding number of shares of the CCXI common stock, on a one -for-one basis. 
 Q. &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; What are the reasons for the structure and timing of the Transactions? 
 A. &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; CCXI is a blank check company formed to effect a merger, amalgamation, share exchange, asset acquisition, stock purchase, reorganization or other similar business combination with one or more businesses. CCXI was incorporated under the laws of the Cayman Islands on June 4, 2025. The Business Combination is the result of extensive work by CCXI, leveraging the Sponsor&#8217;s global network and the investing, operating and transaction experience of CCXI&#8217;s management team and members of the CCXI Board. The terms of the Business Combination are the result of arm&#8217;s -length negotiations between representatives of CCXI and representatives of Agility. 
 On December 16, 2025, CCXI completed its initial public offering. After the CCXI IPO, CCXI commenced an active search for prospective businesses and assets to acquire. In evaluating potential businesses and assets to acquire, CCXI, together with the Sponsor and their advisors, surveyed the landscape of potential acquisition opportunities based on their knowledge of, and familiarity with, the M&amp;A marketplace. In general, CCXI looked for acquisition targets that were of a size relevant to the public marketplace and positioned, operationally and financially, to be successful as a public company. CCXI further looked for those transactions that it believed, if entered, would be well received by the public markets. In particular, CCXI generally sought to identify companies that (i) generate or have the future potential to generate stable free cash -flow , (ii) would benefit uniquely from CCXI&#8217;s capabilities, (iii) are sourced through CCXI&#8217;s proprietary channels, (iv) have a committed and capable management team and (v) have the potential to grow through both organic growth and acquisition opportunities. CCXI also sought to identify companies that it believed would benefit from being a publicly -held entity, particularly with respect to access to capital for both organic growth and for use in acquisitions, with a particular emphasis on opportunities that are primed to unlock disruptive technological advancements. 
 As contemplated by the Merger Agreement, the structure and timing of the Business Combination and the PIPE Investment, are consistent with common practice in initial business combination transactions consummated by special purpose acquisition companies. In addition, the timing for the consummation of the Business Combination provided for in the Merger Agreement and Subscription Agreements, which was effectively as soon as reasonably practicable following the execution of the Merger Agreement, was determined and agreed by the parties in light of general business considerations weighing in favor of consummation the Transactions promptly and the deadline for CCXI to consummate an initial business combination pursuant to the CCXI current articles of association. 
 For more information on structure and timing of the Transactions, see &#8220; Proposal No. 1. &#8212; The Business Combination Proposal &#8212; General&#8221; and &#8220;Proposal No. 1. &#8212; The Business Combination Proposal &#8212; Background of the Transactions .&#8221; 
 Q. &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; What are the material U.S.&#160;federal income tax consequences of the Domestication? 
 A. &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; As discussed more fully under &#8220; Proposal&#160;No.&#160;1 &#8212;&#160;The Business Combination Proposal&#160;&#8212;&#160;Material U.S.&#160;Federal Income Tax Consequences of the Business Combination to CCXI Shareholders &#8221; of this proxy statement/prospectus, CCXI intends for the Domestication to qualify as a reorganization within the meaning of Section&#160;368(a)(1)(F)&#160;of the Code (an &#8220; F Reorganization &#8221;). Assuming that the Domestication so qualifies, and subject to the &#8220;passive foreign investment company&#8221; (&#8220; PFIC &#8221;) rules discussed below and under &#8220; Proposal&#160;No.&#160;1 &#8212;&#160;The Business Combination Proposal&#160;&#8212;&#160;Material U.S.&#160;Federal Income Tax Consequences of the Business Combination to CCXI Shareholders&#160;&#8212;&#160;Tax Effects of the Domestication to U.S.&#160;Holders&#160;&#8212;&#160;PFIC Considerations &#8221; U.S.&#160;Holders (as defined in &#8220; Proposal&#160;No.&#160;1 &#8212;&#160;The Business Combination Proposal&#160;&#8212;&#160;Material U.S.&#160;Federal Income Tax Consequences of the Business Combination to CCXI Shareholders &#8221;) will be subject to Section&#160;367(b)&#160;of the Code in connection with the Domestication and, as a result: 
 &#8226; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; a U.S.&#160;Holder who beneficially owns (directly, indirectly or constructively) 10% or more of the total combined voting power of all classes of CCXI shares entitled to vote or 10% or more of the total value of all classes of CCXI shares (a &#8220; 10% U.S.&#160;Shareholder &#8221;) on the date of the Domestication generally will be 
 

 xx 
 Table of Contents 

 
 required to include in income as a deemed dividend deemed paid by CCXI the &#8220;all earnings and profits amount&#8221; (as defined in the Treasury Regulations under Section&#160;367(b)&#160;of the Code) attributable to the CCXI Class&#160;A Ordinary Shares held directly by such U.S.&#160;Holder; 
 &#8226; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; a U.S.&#160;Holder who, on the date of the Domestication, is not a 10% U.S.&#160;Shareholder and whose CCXI Class&#160;A Ordinary Shares have a fair market value of $50,000 or more on the date of the Domestication generally will recognize gain (but not loss) with respect to its CCXI Class&#160;A Ordinary Shares as if such U.S.&#160;Holder exchanged its CCXI Class&#160;A Ordinary Shares for CCXI common stock in a taxable transaction unless such U.S.&#160;Holder elects in accordance with applicable Treasury Regulations to include in income as a deemed dividend deemed paid by CCXI the &#8220;all earnings and profits&#8221; amount attributable to such U.S.&#160;Holder&#8217;s CCXI Class&#160;A Ordinary Shares; and 
 &#8226; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; a U.S.&#160;Holder who, on the date of the Domestication, is not a 10% U.S.&#160;Shareholder and whose CCXI Class&#160;A Ordinary Shares have a fair market value of less than $50,000 on the date of the Domestication generally will not recognize any gain or loss or include any part of the &#8220;all earnings and profits amount&#8221; in income under Section&#160;367(b)&#160;of the Code in connection with the Domestication. 
 CCXI does not expect to have significant cumulative earnings and profits, if any, on the date of the Domestication. However, the determination of earnings and profits is complex and may be impacted by numerous factors (including matters discussed in this proxy statement/prospectus). It is possible that the amount of CCXI&#8217;s cumulative net earnings and profits could be positive through the date of the Domestication. 
 As discussed more fully under &#8220; Proposal&#160;No.&#160;1 &#8212;&#160;The Business Combination Proposal&#160;&#8212;&#160;Material U.S.&#160;Federal Income Tax Consequences of the Business Combination to CCXI Shareholders&#160;&#8212;&#160;Tax Effects of the Domestication to U.S.&#160;Holders&#160;&#8212;&#160;PFIC Considerations, &#8221; CCXI believes that it is likely classified as a PFIC for U.S.&#160;federal income tax purposes. If CCXI were classified as a PFIC for U.S.&#160;federal income tax purposes, then notwithstanding the U.S.&#160;federal income tax consequences of the Domestication discussed in the foregoing, proposed Treasury Regulations under Section&#160;1291(f)&#160;of the Code and certain other PFIC rules (which have retroactive proposed effective dates), if finalized in their current form, generally would require a U.S.&#160;Holder to recognize gain on the exchange of CCXI Class&#160;A Ordinary Shares for CCXI common stock or CCXI Warrants for CCXI Delaware Warrants pursuant to the Domestication. Any such gain would be taxable income with no corresponding receipt of cash in the Domestication. The tax on any such gain would be imposed at the rate applicable to ordinary income and an interest charge would apply based on a complex set of rules. The proposed Treasury Regulations provide coordinating rules with other sections of the Code, including Section&#160;367(b), which affect the manner in which the rules under such other sections apply to transfers of PFIC stock. However, it is difficult to predict whether, in what form, and with what effective date, final Treasury Regulations under Section&#160;1291(f)&#160;of the Code and such other PFIC rules may be adopted and how any such Treasury Regulations would apply. Importantly, however, U.S.&#160;Holders that make or have made certain elections discussed further under &#8220; Proposal&#160;No.&#160;1 &#8212;&#160;The Business Combination Proposal&#160;&#8212;&#160;Material U.S.&#160;Federal Income Tax Consequences of the Business Combination to CCXI Shareholders&#160;&#8212;&#160;Tax Effects of the Domestication to U.S.&#160;Holders&#160;&#8212;&#160;PFIC Considerations &#8221; with respect to their CCXI Class&#160;A Ordinary Shares are generally not subject to the same gain recognition rules under the currently proposed Treasury Regulations under Section&#160;1291(f)&#160;of the Code. Under current law, no such elections may be made with respect to CCXI Warrants. For a more complete discussion of the potential application of the PFIC rules to U.S.&#160;Holders as a result of the Domestication, see &#8220; Proposal&#160;No.&#160;1 &#8212;&#160;The Business Combination Proposal&#160;&#8212;&#160;Material U.S.&#160;Federal Income Tax Consequences of the Business Combination to CCXI Shareholders&#160;&#8212;&#160;Tax Effects of the Domestication to U.S.&#160;Holders&#160;&#8212;&#160;PFIC Considerations. &#8221; 
 Each U.S.&#160;Holder is urged to consult its own tax advisor concerning the application of the PFIC rules, including the proposed Treasury Regulations, to the exchange of CCXI Class&#160;A Ordinary Shares for CCXI common stock and CCXI Warrants for CCXI Delaware Warrants pursuant to the Domestication. 
 Moreover, U.S.&#160;Holders of CCXI public shares exercising redemption rights will be subject to the potential tax consequences of the Domestication. 
 Additionally, the Domestication may cause Non -U .S.&#160;Holders (as defined in &#8220; Proposal&#160;No.&#160;1 &#8212;&#160;The Business Combination Proposal&#160;&#8212;&#160;Material U.S.&#160;Federal Income Tax Consequences of the Business Combination to CCXI Shareholders &#8221;) to become subject to U.S.&#160;federal withholding taxes on any amounts treated as dividends paid in respect of such Non -U .S.&#160;Holder&#8217;s Agility common stock after the Domestication.

 A. &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; There are a number of closing conditions in the Merger Agreement, including the expiration or termination of the applicable waiting period under the HSR Act and the approval by CCXI shareholders of the business combination proposal, the domestication proposal, the organizational documents proposal, the advisory organizational documents proposal, the stock issuance proposal, the incentive plan proposal, the ESPP proposal and the director election proposal. For a summary of the conditions that must be satisfied or waived prior to completion of the business combination, please see the section entitled &#8220; Proposal&#160;No.&#160;1 &#8212;&#160;The Business Combination Proposal&#160;&#8212;&#160;Certain Agreements Related to the Business Combination&#160;&#8212;&#160;Merger Agreement&#160;&#8212;&#160;Conditions to Closing General Conditions .&#8221;

 A. &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; The obligations of Agility to consummate the business combination are conditioned upon, among others, the Available Closing SPAC Cash being at least $200&#160;million.

 Q. &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; What happens if&#160;I sell my CCXI Class&#160;A Ordinary Shares before the extraordinary general meeting? 
 A. &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; The record date for the extraordinary general meeting is earlier than the date that the business combination is expected to be completed. If you transfer your CCXI Class&#160;A Ordinary Shares after the CCXI record date, but before the extraordinary general meeting, unless the transferee obtains from you a proxy to vote those shares, you will retain your right to vote at the extraordinary general meeting. However, you will not be able to seek redemption of your CCXI public shares because you will no longer be able to deliver them for cancellation upon consummation of the business combination. If you transfer your CCXI Class&#160;A Ordinary Shares prior to the CCXI record date, you will have no right to vote those shares at the extraordinary general meeting or redeem CCXI public shares for a pro rata portion of the funds held in the trust account net of permitted withdrawals. 
 Q. &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; What constitutes a quorum at the extraordinary general meeting? 
 A. &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; At least one -third (1/3) of the paid up voting share capital of CCXI entitled to vote as of the CCXI record date at the extraordinary general meeting must be present by attendance via the virtual meeting website, or represented by proxy, at the extraordinary general meeting to constitute a quorum and in order to conduct business at the extraordinary general meeting. Abstentions will be considered present for the purposes of establishing a quorum but, as a matter of Cayman Islands law, will not constitute votes cast at the extraordinary general meeting and therefore will have no effect on the approval of each of the proposals as a matter of Cayman Islands law. As of the CCXI record date, the close of business on &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;, 2026, &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; CCXI Ordinary Shares would be required to be present at the extraordinary general meeting to achieve a quorum. 
 The CCXI current articles of association permit the chair of the extraordinary general meeting to adjourn the extraordinary general meeting, from time to time and from place to place either (1)&#160;with the consent of any general meeting at which a quorum is present (and shall if so directed by the meeting); or (2)&#160;without the consent of such meeting if, in his or her sole opinion, he or she considers it necessary to do so to: (a)&#160;secure the orderly conduct or proceedings of the meeting; or (b)&#160;give all persons present in person or by proxy and having the right to speak and/or vote at such meeting, the ability to do so. No business shall be transacted at any adjourned meeting other than the business left unfinished at the meeting from which the adjournment took place. When a meeting, or adjourned meeting, is adjourned for fourteen (14)&#160;days or more, notice of the adjourned meeting shall be given in the manner provided for the original meeting. Save as aforesaid, it shall not be necessary to give any notice of an adjournment or of the business to be transacted at an adjourned meeting.

 Q. &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; What vote is required to approve the proposals presented at the extraordinary general meeting? 
 A. &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; The approval of each of the business combination proposal, the advisory organizational documents proposal, the stock issuance proposal, the incentive plan proposal, the ESPP proposal, the director election proposal and, if presented, the adjournment proposal require approval by ordinary resolution, being the affirmative vote of a simple majority of the votes cast by holders of outstanding CCXI Ordinary Shares represented at the extraordinary general meeting by attendance via the virtual meeting website, in person or by proxy and entitled to vote at the extraordinary general meeting, voting together as a single class. Accordingly, if a valid quorum is established, a CCXI shareholder&#8217;s failure to vote by proxy or to vote at the extraordinary general meeting with regard to the business combination proposal, the advisory organizational documents proposal, the stock issuance proposal, the incentive plan proposal, the ESPP proposal, the director election proposal and, if presented, the adjournment proposal will have no effect on such proposals. The business combination proposal does not require the approval of a majority of the unaffiliated holders of CCXI Ordinary Shares. Prior to the closing of an initial business combination, the CCXI current articles of association prescribe that only holders of CCXI Class&#160;B Ordinary Shares are entitled to appoint and remove directors. Accordingly, the director election proposal is being voted on by CCXI shareholders on a non -binding advisory basis only. 
 The approval of the domestication proposal and the organizational documents proposal require approval by special resolution, being the affirmative vote of holders of at least two -thirds of the CCXI Ordinary Shares represented at the extraordinary general meeting by attendance via the virtual meeting website, in person or by proxy and entitled to vote at the extraordinary general meeting, voting together as a single class. Accordingly, if a valid quorum is established, a CCXI shareholder&#8217;s failure to vote by proxy or to vote at the extraordinary general meeting with regard to the domestication proposal and the organizational documents proposal will have no effect on such proposals. Under the CCXI current articles of association, CCXI&#8217;s directors have the authority to resolve that CCXI be registered by way of continuation in a jurisdiction outside the Cayman Islands or such other jurisdiction in which it is for the time being incorporated, registered or existing (including, but not limited to, the approval of the organizational documents to be adopted by the Company in such other jurisdiction to the extent applicable). Accordingly, it is not necessary for CCXI to receive shareholder consent to the Domestication, and the domestication proposal and the organizational documents proposal are therefore being presented to CCXI shareholders on a non -binding advisory basis only. 
 Q. &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; How many votes do&#160;I have at the extraordinary general meeting? 
 A.&#160; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; CCXI shareholders are entitled to one vote on each proposal presented at the extraordinary general meeting for each share of CCXI Ordinary Shares held of record as of the close of business on &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; , 2026, the record date for the extraordinary general meeting. As of the close of business on the CCXI record date, there were &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; outstanding CCXI Class&#160;A Ordinary Shares and &#160;&#160;&#160; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; outstanding CCXI Class&#160;B Ordinary Shares. 
 Q. &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Why is CCXI proposing the advisory organizational documents proposal? 
 A. &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; As required by applicable SEC guidance, CCXI is requesting that its shareholders vote upon, on a non -binding advisory basis, a proposal to approve certain governance provisions contained in the Proposed Certificate of Incorporation that materially affect shareholder rights. This separate vote is not otherwise required by Delaware law separate and apart from the organizational documents proposal, but pursuant to SEC guidance, CCXI is required to submit these provisions to its shareholders separately for approval. However, the shareholder vote regarding this proposal is an advisory vote, and is not binding on CCXI and the CCXI Board (separate and apart from the approval of the charter proposal). Furthermore, the business combination is not conditioned on the separate approval of the advisory organizational documents proposal (separate and apart from approval of the organizational documents proposal). Please see the section entitled &#8220; Proposal&#160;No.&#160;4 &#8212;&#160;The Advisory Organizational Documents Proposal .&#8221; 
 Q. &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Do&#160;I have redemption rights? 
 A. &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; If you are a holder of CCXI public shares, you have the right to demand that CCXI redeem such shares for cash in an amount equal to the pro rata portion of the funds held in the trust account, net of permitted withdrawals. CCXI sometimes refers to these rights to demand redemption of CCXI public shares as &#8220; redemption rights .&#8221; Redemption rights in connection with a vote to approve the business combination are not available to our Sponsor, directors and officers.

 Notwithstanding the foregoing, a holder of CCXI public shares, together with any affiliate of such holder or any other person with whom such holder is acting in concert or as a &#8220;group&#8221; (as defined in Section&#160;13(d)(3)&#160;of the Exchange&#160;Act), will be restricted from seeking redemption with respect to more than 15% of the CCXI public shares. Accordingly, all CCXI public shares in excess of 15% held by a CCXI public shareholder, together with any affiliate of such holder or any other person with whom such holder is acting in concert or as a &#8220;group,&#8221; will not be redeemed without the prior written consent of our directors. 
 Under the Exchange&#160;Act, the business combination may be consummated only if CCXI has at least $5,000,001 of net tangible assets after giving effect to all holders of CCXI public shares that properly demand redemption of their shares for cash on the date that is two&#160;business days prior to the date of the extraordinary general meeting. 
 Pursuant to the Sponsor Agreement, the Sponsor and the Insiders have agreed to waive their redemption rights with respect to all of their CCXI Ordinary Shares in connection with the consummation of the business combination and, because of this, such CCXI Ordinary Shares are excluded from the pro rata calculation used to determine the per share redemption price. As is customary in transactions of this type, the Sponsor and the Insiders did not receive any consideration for waiving their redemption rights. 
 Q. &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; How do&#160;I exercise my redemption rights? 
 A. &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; If you are a holder of CCXI public shares and wish to exercise your redemption rights, you must demand that CCXI redeem your shares in cash no later than 5:00&#160;p.m. Eastern time on &#160;&#160;&#160; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; , 2026, the second business&#160;day preceding the extraordinary general meeting vote on the business combination proposal (or such later date as may be determined by our directors), by delivering your stock to Continental Stock Transfer&#160;&amp; Trust Company, CCXI&#8217;s transfer agent, physically or electronically using Depository Trust Company&#8217;s Deposit and Withdrawal at Custodian (&#8220; DWAC &#8221;) System and requesting in writing that we redeem your CCXI public shares for cash to Continental Stock Transfer&#160;&amp; Trust Company, CCXI&#8217;s transfer agent, at the following address: One State Street 30 th Floor, New&#160;York, New&#160;York 10004. Any holder of CCXI public shares will be entitled to demand that such holder&#8217;s shares be redeemed for cash in an amount equal to their pro rata portion of the funds held in the trust account, including interest earned on the funds held in the trust account (which interest shall be net of permitted withdrawals), which, for illustrative purposes, was approximately $&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; or $&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; per share, as of the CCXI record date. Such amount will be paid promptly upon consummation of the business combination. However, the funds held in the trust account could be subject to claims of creditors which could take priority over those of CCXI public shareholders exercising redemption rights, regardless of whether such holders vote for or against the business combination proposal. Therefore, the per share distribution from the trust account in such a situation may be less than originally anticipated due to such claims. Your vote on any proposal other than the business combination proposal will have no impact on the amount you will receive upon exercise of your redemption rights. 
 Any request for redemption, once made by a holder of CCXI public shares, may be withdrawn at any time up to the time the vote is taken with respect to the business combination proposal at the extraordinary general meeting. If you deliver your CCXI public shares for redemption to CCXI&#8217;s transfer agent and later decide prior to the extraordinary general meeting not to elect redemption, you may request that CCXI&#8217;s transfer agent return the shares (physically or electronically). You may make such request by contacting CCXI&#8217;s transfer agent at the address listed at the end of this section. 
 Any corrected or changed proxy card or written demand of redemption rights must be received by CCXI&#8217;s transfer agent at least two&#160;business days prior to the initially scheduled vote taken on the business combination proposal at the extraordinary general meeting or such later date as our board of directors may determine. No demand for redemption will be honored unless the holder&#8217;s stock has been delivered (either physically or electronically) to the transfer agent at least two&#160;business days prior to the initially scheduled vote at the extraordinary general meeting. 
 If a redemption demand is properly made as described above, then, if the business combination is consummated, CCXI will redeem such CCXI public shares for a pro rata portion of funds held in the trust account. If you exercise your redemption rights, then you will be exchanging your CCXI public shares for cash.

 Q. &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; If&#160;I am a holder of CCXI public units or CCXI public shares, can&#160;I exercise redemption rights with respect to my CCXI public warrants? 
 A. &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; No. Beginning on February&#160;9, 2026, holders of CCXI public units issued in the CCXI IPO were given the option to elect to separately trade their CCXI public shares and CCXI public warrants included in their CCXI public units. Any CCXI public units not separated continue to trade on Nasdaq under the symbol &#8220;CCXIU.&#8221; Holders of CCXI public units, or, if separated, CCXI public shares who still hold CCXI public warrants, have no redemption rights with respect to the CCXI public warrants. Therefore, if any such holder has exercised their right to redeem their CCXI public units or CCXI public shares, such holder will still own CCXI public warrants prior to the Closing and, after the Closing, Post -Closing Company public warrants, unless such holder has otherwise elected to sell such warrants. 
 Q. &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; How do the CCXI public warrants differ from the CCXI private placement warrants, and what are the related risks for holders of CCXI public warrants after the business combination? 
 A. &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; The CCXI public warrants are identical to the CCXI private placement warrants in all material terms and provisions, except that, unlike the CCXI public warrants, the CCXI private placement warrants (including the shares of CCXI Class&#160;A Ordinary Shares issuable upon exercise of the CCXI private placement warrants) are not redeemable by CCXI (or, upon Closing, the Post -Closing Company), CCXI private placement warrants will not expire except upon liquidation and the holders of CCXI private placement warrants have the right to exercise such warrants on a &#8220;cashless basis&#8221; (whereas the holders of CCXI public warrants cannot do so unless required by CCXI under certain circumstances). The CCXI public warrants will expire five&#160;years after the completion of the business combination, at 5:00&#160;p.m., New&#160;York City time, or earlier upon redemption or liquidation. See the section entitled &#8220; Description of Securities&#160;&#8212;&#160;Warrants &#8221; for more information regarding the CCXI public warrants and the CCXI private placement warrants. 
 Upon the Closing, the Post -Closing Company public warrants and Post -Closing Company private placement warrants will have the same rights as the CCXI public warrants and CCXI private placement warrants, respectively. Following the Closing, the Post -Closing Company may redeem your unexpired Post -Closing Company public warrants prior to their exercise at a time that is disadvantageous to you, making your warrants worthless. The Post -Closing Company may redeem outstanding Post -Closing Company public warrants at any time after they become exercisable and prior to their expiration, at a price of $0.01 per Post -Closing Company public warrant. To exercise such redemption right: (1)&#160;the last reported sale price of Post -Closing Company common stock must equal or exceed $18.00 per share (as adjusted for share subdivisions, share dividends, reorganizations, recapitalizations and the like) for any 20&#160;trading days within a 30 trading -day period ending on the third&#160;trading day prior to the date on which we send notice of redemption to the warrant holders; and (2)&#160;certain other conditions must be met. If and when the Post -Closing Company public warrants become redeemable by the Post -Closing Company, we may exercise our redemption right even if we are unable to register or qualify the underlying securities for sale under all applicable state securities laws. As a result, the Post -Closing Company may redeem the Post -Closing Company public warrants as set forth above even if the holders are otherwise unable to exercise the Post -Closing Company public warrants. Redemption of the outstanding Public Warrants could force you to: (1)&#160;exercise your Post -Closing Company public warrants and pay the exercise price at a time when it may be disadvantageous for you to do so; (2)&#160;sell your Post -Closing Company public warrants at the then -current market price when you might otherwise wish to hold your Post -Closing Company public warrants; or (3)&#160;accept the nominal redemption price which, at the time the outstanding Post -Closing Company public warrants are called for redemption, is likely to be substantially less than the market value of your Post -Closing Company public warrants. Please see &#8220; Risk Factors&#160;&#8212;&#160;Risk Related to CCXI, the Domestication and the Business Combination&#160;&#8212;&#160;CCXI may redeem your unexpired CCXI public warrants prior to their exercise at a time that is disadvantageous to you, thereby making your warrants without value to the holder .&#8221; 
 If the Post -Closing Company calls the Post -Closing Company public warrants for redemption, management of the Post -Closing Company will have the option to require all holders that wish to exercise the Post -Closing Company public warrants to do so on a &#8220;cashless basis,&#8221; as described in the section entitled &#8220; Description of Securities&#160;&#8212;&#160;Warrants &#8221; and the CCXI public warrant agreement, a copy of which is attached as an exhibit to the registration statement of which this proxy statement/prospectus is a part. The exercise price and number of shares of the Post -Closing Company common stock issuable upon exercise of the Post -Closing Company public warrants may be adjusted in certain circumstances including in the event of a share dividend, or recapitalization, reorganization, merger or consolidation. However, the Post -Closing Company public warrants will not be adjusted for issuance of the Post -Closing Company common stock at a price below its exercise price. Additionally, in no event will the Post -Closing Company be required to net cash settle the Post -Closing Company public warrants.
