 This is not a capability we are forecasting for the first time. Through engineering improvements, supplier engagement, manufacturing experience and increasing production scale, Agility has already reduced the bill of materials for Digit v4 to approximately $125,000 per robot. These same operating disciplines are now being applied to Digit v5. 
 Digit v5 is not a concept or a design on paper. We have already built and produced Digit v5&#160;prototype units, which we expect to release in late 2026, and our early manufacturing experience is validating the cost reduction roadmap developed for the platform. While meaningful cost reductions have already been achieved, we continue to identify additional opportunities across engineering, supply chain and manufacturing that we believe will substantially reduce the bill of materials over time. We believe that this repeatable process of engineering innovation, manufacturing learning and supply chain optimization will continue to strengthen both customer economics and Agility&#8217;s long -term financial performance. 
 A Platform for Long-Term Growth 
 Humanoid robotics remains in the early stages of commercialization. Agility has established an initial commercial focus in manufacturing, distribution and logistics, where persistent labor shortages, compelling customer economics and environments designed for people create an attractive entry point for humanoid robotics. We believe the introduction of Digit v5, with its cooperative safety architecture and expanded capabilities, will represent an important step toward broader commercial adoption. As Digit&#8217;s capabilities continue to evolve and deployments expand, we believe the Agility platform is well positioned to support a growing number of customers, workflows, industries and end markets. 
 Our long -term growth strategy is centered on five complementary initiatives: expanding our customer base, growing with existing customers, expanding Digit&#8217;s capabilities, broadening the Agility platform and extending humanoid robotics into new markets over time. 
 Growing our customer base. 
 Agility continues to expand its commercial customer base through direct customer engagement and the CAP, which enables prospective customers to evaluate Digit within their own operations before broader deployment. This phased approach reduces implementation risk, demonstrates customer value and establishes long -term commercial relationships. As awareness of humanoid robotics continues to increase and customers gain confidence in the technology, we believe these programs position Agility to continue adding leading enterprise customers across manufacturing, distribution and logistics. As of May&#160;2026, Agility has signed four new customers to the CAP and was engaged with more than 30 prospective customers through active commercial discussions and the CAP. 
 Growing with existing customers. 
 Initial deployments are typically focused on validating operational performance and customer economics within a limited number of workflows and facilities. As customers gain confidence in Digit&#8217;s capabilities and realize measurable operational benefits, we believe deployments can expand through greater deployment density within existing facilities, additional workflows, replication across multiple customer sites and ultimately broader enterprise -wide adoption. This land -and-expand strategy has the potential to significantly increase the number of deployed robots within existing customer relationships while strengthening long -term strategic partnerships. As of May&#160;2026, we have secured $300&#160;million of multi -year orders for Digit v5 subject to the satisfaction of certain contractual milestones, product features and/or specifications, with a potential commercial pipeline multiple times that amount. These orders relate to 1,000 Digit v5 robots under a three -year term RaaS contract, which includes warrants issued to the purchaser that vest proportionately as robots are deployed. 
 Expanding Digit&#8217;s capabilities. 
 Every improvement to Digit expands the range of useful physical labor the platform can perform. Today, commercial deployments are focused primarily on repetitive material handling workflows such as moving bins and totes. As advances in embodied AI, manipulation, perception and cooperative safety continue, we expect customers to deploy the same robot across a broader range of workflows, including each picking, kitting, carton handling and other increasingly complex physical tasks. Expanding the range of work Digit can perform increases robot utilization, strengthens customer economics and enhances the value of every deployment.

 Broadening the Agility platform. 
 As Digit deployments increase, we expect our installed base to generate an expanding stream of recurring software and services revenue. As customers deploy larger fleets, we expect increasing demand for software, deployment services, spare parts, maintenance and other lifecycle support. Together, we expect these offerings to deepen customer relationships while expanding recurring revenue opportunities over time. 
 Beyond these recurring services, we believe additional opportunities exist to commercialize technologies developed across the Agility platform. Agility Arc was designed as an enterprise deployment platform that integrates robots with warehouse management systems, manufacturing execution systems and other automation technologies, and we are evaluating opportunities to expand its commercialization over time. We are also actively evaluating strategic partnerships and licensing opportunities for certain proprietary technologies, including our cycloidal actuators, where doing so can accelerate industry adoption while creating additional sources of revenue. 
 Expanding the addressable market. 
 Manufacturing, distribution and logistics represent the beginning of Agility&#8217;s long -term opportunity rather than the limits of the market we seek to serve. Digit v5 was designed to expand the range of commercial environments in which humanoid robots can operate by advancing three critical capabilities: cooperative safety, dexterity and autonomy. 
 Together, these capabilities enable Digit to perform a broader range of physical work while operating safely alongside trained personnel in active industrial environments. We believe these advancements have the potential to significantly expand Agility&#8217;s future addressable market beyond our initial beachhead deployments into additional workflows and industries, including grocery distribution, reverse logistics, electronics manufacturing, pharmaceutical manufacturing, machining, construction, agriculture and other industrial applications where organizations face persistent labor shortages and repetitive physical work. 
 As Digit continues to acquire new capabilities, we expect customers to deploy the same platform across an expanding range of workflows within existing facilities before extending deployments into adjacent industries. We believe this progression increases customer value, strengthens return on investment and expands Agility&#8217;s commercial opportunity over time. 
 Looking ahead. 
 Agility&#8217;s commercialization strategy begins by solving today&#8217;s industrial labor challenges, where customer demand, measurable economics and technology readiness are already aligned. Every commercial deployment strengthens the Agility platform through operational experience, engineering innovation and continuous improvement, enabling Digit to perform increasingly sophisticated forms of useful physical labor. 
 We believe this progression creates a natural pathway beyond today&#8217;s industrial applications. As advances in embodied AI, manipulation, cooperative safety and autonomy continue, we believe that humanoid robots will become capable of operating in increasingly dynamic environments, interacting with broader populations and ultimately assisting people in everyday life. By beginning with focused industrial deployments and continuously expanding Digit&#8217;s capabilities over time, Agility believes it is building the technological foundation for robot partners that can ultimately become part of the home.

 Overview 
 Agility Robotics, Inc. was founded in 2015 out of the Oregon State University Robotics Institute with initial funding from DARPA and has spent more than a decade advancing humanoids into real -world commercial deployment. Headquartered in Salem, Oregon, our mission is to build robot partners that augment the human workforce, ultimately enabling humans to be more human. 
 Agility&#8217;s solutions include Digit, a multi -purpose humanoid robot made for logistics and manufacturing work, and Agility Arc, a cloud automation platform for deploying and managing fleets of Digits. Agility is one of the only humanoid companies with multiple years of operational experience in real customer environments. Digit v4 is performing useful work today for leading enterprises including Schaeffler, GXO, Toyota Motor Manufacturing Canada, and Amazon, with new deployments underway with large blue -chip customers. Digit v5, planned for launch in 2026, is designed as the world&#8217;s first AI -enabled cooperatively safe humanoid. Complementing Digit, Agility Arc, our cloud -based automation platform, is designed to integrate Digit into customer workflows, manage fleets, and optimize operations. 
 Our differentiated business model deploys Digit through both robot deployment arrangements and ownership models, providing customers with flexible adoption paths. The robot deployment model generates recurring revenue streams over an estimated five -year useful life, while building strong customer retention. We have built RoboFab, the world&#8217;s first full -scale humanoid manufacturing facility in Salem, Oregon, designed to produce up to 10,000 Digits annually. Approximately 75% of Digit parts are currently sourced from the U.S., providing cost and availability advantages and supporting domestic manufacturing priorities. We develop our highest -value hardware systems in -house , including proprietary actuators, modular end effectors, whole -body control platform, sensor architecture, system -wide safety, and long -life quick -charge battery configuration. Our proprietary physical AI layer &#8212; combining learned skills, real -time coordination, and physics -based control &#8212; provides scaling performance and cost advantages over competitors reliant on third -party systems. We believe our domestic supply chain and vertically integrated manufacturing approach provides significant competitive advantages in terms of cost, supply security, and production scalability. 
 Recent Developments 
 The Merger Agreement 
 On June&#160;24, 2026, Agility entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger and Reorganization (as amended, modified, supplemented or waived from time to time, the &#8220; Merger Agreement &#8221;) with Churchill Capital Corp&#160;XI (&#8220; CCXI &#8221;), a Cayman Islands exempted company, and BLB Merger Sub, Inc., a Delaware corporation and direct, wholly -owned subsidiary of CCXI (&#8220; Merger Sub &#8221;). The Merger Agreement, among other things and subject to the terms and conditions contained therein, provides for (a)&#160;the transfer of the registration of CCXI by way of continuation from the Cayman Islands to the State of Delaware (the &#8220; Domestication &#8221;), and (b)&#160;following the Domestication, the merger of Merger Sub with and into Agility, with Agility continuing as the surviving corporation, and as a direct wholly owned subsidiary of CCXI (the &#8220; Merger ,&#8221; and together with the Domestication

 and the other transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement and the related agreements, the &#8220; Transactions &#8221; or the &#8220; business combination &#8221;). In connection with the business combination, CCXI will change its name to &#8220;Agility Robotics, Inc.&#8221; 
 While the legal acquirer in the Merger Agreement is CCXI, for financial accounting and reporting purposes under GAAP, Agility will be the accounting acquirer, CCXI will be treated as the &#8220;acquired&#8221; company, and the business combination will be accounted for as a &#8220;reverse recapitalization.&#8221; In accordance with this accounting method, the business combination will be treated as the equivalent of Agility issuing stock for the net assets of CCXI, accompanied by a recapitalization. The net assets of CCXI will be stated at historical cost, which are expected to approximate fair value, with no goodwill or other intangible assets recorded, and operations prior to the business combination will be those of Agility.

 In addition, as a consequence of being a public company, we will need to hire additional personnel and implement procedures and processes to address public company regulatory requirements and customary practices. We expect to incur additional annual expenses as a public company including, among other things, directors&#8217; and officers&#8217; liability insurance, director fees, and additional internal and external accounting, legal, and administrative resources, including increased audit and legal fees.

 Development, Testing and Commercialization of Future Products 
 Our future operating performance will depend on the successful commercialization of our next generation humanoid robots, Digit v5, which we currently expect to begin in 2027.  Customer Adoption and Demand 
 Our long -term growth depends on broader customer adoption of humanoid robotics across warehouse, logistics, manufacturing, and other commercial environments. As our commercial operations grow, we expect our compliance obligations and related costs to increase. 
 In addition, evolving laws, regulations, and industry standards governing robotics, AI, and workplace automation may require changes to our products, deployment practices, or business processes. We continue to invest in our legal, compliance, cybersecurity, and governance capabilities to support our growth and public company obligations; however, changes in the regulatory landscape or our ability to comply with applicable requirements could increase operating costs, delay customer deployments, or otherwise adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations. 
 Components of Results of Operations 
 Net sales 
 Our commercialization strategy is designed to support customers throughout the adoption lifecycle through multiple complementary revenue streams. Net sales are primarily generated through direct sales of Digit humanoid robots and related ancillary hardware, robot deployment arrangements, Customer Acceleration Program (&#8220; CAP &#8221;) engagements, and ongoing support services. 
 Sales of Robotics Equipment 
 Revenue from robotics equipment consists primarily of sales of Digit humanoid robots and related ancillary hardware to customers for their owned use. Revenue from robot sales is recognized at a point in time when control of the robot transfers to the customer, generally upon completion of substantive customer acceptance procedures. Certain robot sale arrangements also include training and software support, which are recognized separately as the related services are provided. 
 

 241 
 Table of Contents 

 
 Deployment and Professional Services 
 Under our robot deployment model, we deploy Digit robots at customer facilities while retaining ownership of the robots and provide customers with access to the deployed systems together with related monitoring, maintenance, software, and support over a defined service term. Revenue is generally recognized ratably over the contractual service period beginning when the deployed robot is operational. While we continue to support direct robot sales where appropriate based on customer requirements and deployment objectives, we expect robot deployment model to become an increasingly important component of our long -term commercialization strategy as it allows customers to deploy robots without a significant upfront capital investment while providing the Company with a recurring revenue stream and ongoing customer engagement. 
 Other professional service revenue is primarily driven by CAP engagements. CAP engagements consist of phased pre -deployment engagements designed to evaluate customer -specific use cases, demonstrate deployment feasibility, and integrate Digit into customer workflows prior to broader commercial deployment. Revenue is recognized over the period the services are performed using a measure of progress that reflects the transfer of the integrated service to the customer. CAP engagements frequently serve as the initial commercial relationship with a customer and are intended to facilitate broader commercial deployment through either direct robot sales or robot deployment arrangements. 
 Repair and Maintenance 
 Revenue from repair, maintenance, parts, and other support services is recognized as goods are delivered or services are performed. Revenue from stand -ready support arrangements, where applicable, is recognized over the related service period. 
 The relative contribution of these revenue streams is expected to evolve over time as customer deployments increase and commercial adoption of our robotic systems expands. 
 Cost of goods sold 
 Cost of products 
 Cost of products primarily consists of materials, labor, freight, manufacturing overhead, depreciation of manufacturing assets, and inventory reserves, including charges associated with obsolete robot models, incurred in the production and sale of Digit robots and related ancillary hardware. Cost of products is recorded when the control of products is transferred to the customer. 
 Cost of services 
 Cost of services consists primarily of personnel -related costs, including salaries, benefits and stock based compensation, materials, depreciation, and other direct costs associated with CAP engagements, robot deployment arrangements, and repair, maintenance, and other support services. Cost of services is recognized as the related services are performed. 
 Selling, general and administrative expenses 
 Selling expenses primarily consist of personnel -related costs, including salaries, commissions, benefits and stock -based compensation, for employees performing bid, proposal, marketing and sales functions as well as allocations of facility and consulting costs. General and administrative expenses primarily consist of personnel -related costs, including salaries, benefits and stock -based compensation, for executive leadership and employees in legal, finance, accounting, human resources, information technology and other administrative functions as well as allocated facility and consulting costs. 
 Research and development expenses 
 Research and development expenses primarily consist of personnel -related costs, including salaries, benefits and stock -based compensation, costs of materials, costs of consultants and allocated facility costs associated with the research, engineering, design and development of our next generation humanoid robots.

 Interest income 
 Interest income, net consists primarily of interest earned on interest -bearing cash deposits and short -term , highly liquid investments. 
 Other, net 
 Other income (expense) is composed primarily of credit card rebates and employee retention credits, offset by losses on the sale of property and equipment.

 Net Sales&#160;&#8212;&#160;Trade 
 Net sales&#160;&#8212;&#160;trade increased by $0.4&#160;million, or 136%, to $0.7&#160;million for the year ended December&#160;31, 2025 from $0.3&#160;million for the year ended December&#160;31, 2024. The increase was primarily driven by $0.5&#160;million of increased additional robot sales. 
 Net Sales&#160;&#8212;&#160;Related Parties 
 Net sales to related parties increased by $1.1&#160;million, or 3,229%, to $1.1&#160;million for the year ended December&#160;31, 2025 from $0 for the year ended December&#160;31, 2024. The increase was primarily driven by sales of Digit robots to one investor during 2025. 
 Cost of Goods Sold 
 Cost of goods sold increased by $4.0 million, or 866%, to $4.5 million for the year ended December 31, 2025 from $0.5 million for the year ended December 31, 2024. This increase was primarily driven by approximately $2.1 million of increased labor and overhead costs allocated to cost of goods sold, $1.6 million of additional product costs associated with increased robot sales, and $0.4 million of increased costs related to our robot deployment arrangements. Gross margins remained negative as the Company continues to operate at an early stage of commercialization and is continuing to scale manufacturing operations and production efficiencies.

 Selling, General and Administrative 
 Selling, general and administrative increased by $29.6 million, or 183%, to $45.8 million for the year ended December 31, 2025 from $16.2 million for the year ended December 31, 2024. The increase is primarily driven by approximately $15.3 million of increased stock -based compensation expense tied to increased valuation of the liability classified awards that need to be mark -to-market adjusted each period end, $5.2 million of increased personnel -related costs associated with expanding commercial and corporate functions, and $4.0 million of investments in sales and marketing activities and corporate infrastructure supporting commercialization activities. 
 Research and Development 
 Research and development increased by $38.2 million, or 72%, to $91.6 million for the year ended December 31, 2025 from $53.4 million for the year ended December 31, 2024. The increase was primarily driven by approximately $21.5 million of increased stock -based compensation expense tied to increased valuation of the liability classified awards that need to be mark -to-market adjusted each period end, $8.1 million of increased outside R&amp;D services related to the development of the Company&#8217;s Digit v5 robot, and $7.1 million of increased personnel -related costs tied to expanding R&amp;D resources. 
 Other Income (Expense)

 Critical Accounting Policies and Estimates 
 Our consolidated financial statements included in this proxy statement/prospectus have been prepared in accordance with GAAP.&#160;Preparation of the financial statements requires our management to make judgments, estimates and assumptions that impact the reported amounts of net sales and expenses, assets and liabilities and the disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities. We consider an accounting judgment, estimate or assumption to be critical when the estimate or assumption is complex in nature or requires a high degree of judgment and the use of different judgments, estimates and assumptions could have a material impact on our consolidated financial statements. We periodically review estimates and adjusts those estimates when facts and circumstances dictate. To the extent that there are material differences between these estimates and actual results, its financial condition or results of operations will be affected. 
 While our significant accounting policies are described in Note&#160;2 to our audited financial statements included elsewhere in this proxy statement/prospectus, we believe the following critical accounting policies are most important to understanding and evaluating our reported financial results. 
 Revenue Recognition 
 We recognize revenue from sales of robotics equipment, robot deployment arrangements, CAP engagements, and repair, maintenance, and other support services. Certain customer arrangements, particularly CAP engagements and contracts with multiple performance obligations, require management to exercise judgment in determining the timing of revenue recognition and the allocation of transaction price to the related performance obligations. 
 Management also exercises judgment in estimating variable consideration, including customer incentives and other contractual adjustments, and in assessing progress toward completion for revenue recognized over time. These estimates are based on the specific terms of each customer arrangement and management&#8217;s expectations regarding contract performance. Changes in these estimates could affect the timing and amount of revenue recognized in future periods. 
 Inventory 
 Inventories are stated at the lower of average cost or net realizable value and consist primarily of raw materials and work in process. Management exercises judgment in determining inventory valuation, including the allocation of manufacturing costs to inventory and the estimation of excess and obsolete inventory reserves. 
 

 246 
 Table of Contents 

 
 The determination of excess and obsolete inventory requires management to evaluate expected future demand, product lifecycle assumptions, engineering compatibility of components across robot models, and the expected recoverability of inventory through future production and commercial deployment. Management also evaluates whether materials are associated with commercial production activities or research and development efforts, as materials determined to be used solely for research and development are expensed as incurred. Changes in these assumptions could materially affect inventory valuation and the amount of inventory -related expense recognized in future periods. 
 Property and Equipment 
 Property and equipment consists primarily of robots deployed under robot deployment arrangements, construction in progress, and manufacturing equipment. Management exercises judgment in determining when internally manufactured robots are transferred from inventory into property and equipment and when those robots are considered placed into service, at which time depreciation begins. 
 Management also exercises judgment in estimating the useful lives of robots and evaluating those assets for impairment. These estimates require consideration of expected deployment periods, product lifecycle assumptions, technological obsolescence, and expected future economic benefit. Changes in these assumptions could result in changes to estimated useful lives or the recognition of impairment charges in future periods. 
 Contingently Redeemable Preferred Stock 
 As all series of our preferred stock are contingently redeemable upon the occurrence of events not solely within our control, the preferred stock is presented as mezzanine equity, separate from the stockholders&#8217; deficit section of the consolidated balance sheet. The preferred stock is initially recorded at the fair value determined on the issuance date. Adjustments to the fair value of the preferred stock to the current market value are not made each period. Rather, we assess whether the contingently redeemable preferred stock has become redeemable or the probability that the preferred stock will become redeemable in determining whether to record subsequent measurement adjustments. 
 The Company&#8217;s Series&#160;A, A -1 , A -2 , A -3 , A -4 , B, B, C -1 and C -2 Preferred Stock are not currently redeemable or probable of becoming redeemable in the future period. Refer to Note&#160;8 to our audited consolidated financial statements included elsewhere in this proxy statement/prospectus for additional information. 
 Stock-Based Compensation 
 The Company grants stock options under its Equity Incentive Plan, which are accounted for as liability -classified awards due to the Company&#8217;s contractual repurchase rights associated with exercised awards. Liability -classified awards are initially measured at fair value on the grant date and subsequently remeasured to fair value at each reporting date until settlement or until the repurchase right lapse and the awards are no longer require liability classification. Changes in fair value are recognized as stock -based compensation expense and allocated between cost of goods sold, selling, general, and administrative expenses, and research and development expenses in the statement of operations, based on the function of the employees to whom the expense relates. 
 The determination of the fair value of liability -classified awards requires significant judgment. Because the Company&#8217;s common stock is not publicly traded, the fair value of the underlying common stock is determined based on periodic independent third -party valuations that consider recent equity transactions, the Company&#8217;s operating and financial performance, comparable companies, market conditions, and other relevant factors. The fair value of the awards is estimated using the Black -Scholes option -pricing model, which incorporates assumptions including the expected term, expected volatility, risk -free interest rate, and expected dividend yield. Changes in these assumptions or in the estimated fair value of the Company&#8217;s common stock could materially affect the amount of stock -based compensation expense recognized in future periods. The Company accounts for forfeitures as they occur.

 Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk 
 Interest Rate Risk 
 We had cash and cash equivalents of $103&#160;million as of December&#160;31, 2025. We hold our cash and cash equivalents for working capital purposes. Our cash and cash equivalents are held in cash deposits and money market funds. 
 Due to the short -term nature of these instruments, we believe that we do not have any material exposure to changes in the fair value of cash and cash equivalents and available -for-sale securities due to changes in interest rates. Increasing interest rates, however, would reduce the value of our available -for-sale securities and declining interest rates would reduce our future interest income. The effect of a hypothetical 10% change in interest rates would not have a material impact on our financial statements. 
 Concentrations of Credit Risk 
 We deposit cash with financial institutions, and, at times, such balances may exceed federally insured limits. We believe the financial institutions that hold our cash and cash equivalents are financially sound and, accordingly, minimal credit risk exists with respect to cash and cash equivalents. 
 Emerging Growth Company Status 
 Section&#160;102(b)(1)&#160;of the JOBS Act exempts emerging growth companies from being required to comply with new or revised financial accounting standards until private companies are required to comply with the new or revised financial accounting standards. The JOBS Act provides that a company can choose not to take advantage of the extended transition period and comply with the requirements that apply to non -emerging growth companies, and any such election to not take advantage of the extended transition period is irrevocable. The Post -Closing Company intends to take advantage of the benefits of this extended transition period and, following the consummation of the business combination, will be an emerging growth company (for the period described in the immediately succeeding paragraph) and will take advantage of the benefits of the extended transition period emerging growth company status permits. During the extended transition period, it may be difficult or impossible to compare the Post -Closing Company&#8217;s financial results with the financial results of another public company that complies with public company effective dates for accounting standard updates because of the potential differences in accounting standards used: 
 The Post -Closing Company will remain an emerging growth company under the JOBS Act until the earlier of: 
 &#8226; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; The last&#160;day of the fiscal year in which its total annual gross revenues are $1.235&#160;billion or more. 
 &#8226; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; The last&#160;day of the fiscal year following the fifth anniversary of the CCXI IPO. 
 &#8226; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; The date on which it has issued more than $1.0&#160;billion in non -convertible debt during the previous three&#160;years. 
 &#8226; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; The date on which it is deemed to be a large accelerated filer.

 CCXI Executive Officer and Director Compensation 
 CCXI is an &#8220;emerging growth company,&#8221; as defined in the JOBS Act, and the following is intended to comply with the reduced disclosure requirements applicable to emerging growth companies. No executive officer of CCXI has received any cash compensation for services rendered to CCXI although CCXI may pay consulting, finder or success fees to its officers, directors, or shareholders (or their affiliates) for assisting it in consummating its initial business combination. These officers, directors and shareholders will receive reimbursement for any out -of-pocket expenses incurred by them in connection with activities on CCXI&#8217;s behalf, such as identifying potential target businesses, performing business due diligence on suitable target businesses and business combinations, as well as traveling to and from the offices, plants, or similar locations of prospective target businesses to examine their operations. 
 After the business combination, any members of CCXI&#8217;s management team who remain with the Post -Closing Company may be paid consulting, management, or other fees from the Post -Closing Company.  The Post-Closing Company Executive Officer and Director Compensation Following the Business Combination 
 Following the Closing, the Post -Closing Company intends to develop an executive and director compensation program that is designed to align compensation with the Post -Closing Company&#8217;s business objectives and the creation of stockholder value, while enabling the Post -Closing Company to attract, retain, incentivize and reward individuals who contribute to the long -term success of the Post -Closing Company. 
 Executive Compensation 
 The policies of the Post -Closing Company with respect to the compensation of its executive officers and following the business combination will be administered by the Post -Closing Company Board in consultation with its compensation committee. We expect that the compensation policies followed by the Post -Closing Company will be designed to provide for compensation that is sufficient to attract, motivate and retain executives of the Post -Closing Company and to establish an appropriate relationship between executive compensation and the creation of stockholder value. 
 In addition to the guidance provided by its compensation committee, the Post -Closing Company Board may utilize the services of third parties from time to time in connection with the hiring and determination of compensation awarded to executive employees. The Post -Closing Company is currently negotiating the terms of new employment agreements with the individuals that are expected to become the senior executive officers of the Post -Closing Company. 
 Director Compensation 
 We intend to adopt a non -employee director compensation policy, effective as of the Closing, pursuant to which our non -employee directors will be eligible to receive compensation for service on our board of directors and committees of our board of directors.

 Rule&#160;10b5-1 Sales Plans 
 The directors and executive officers of the Post -Closing Company may adopt written plans, known as Rule&#160;10b5 -1 plans (&#8220; Rule&#160;10b5 -1 Plans &#8221;), in which they will contract with a broker to buy or sell shares of our common stock on a periodic basis. Under a Rule&#160;10b5 -1 Plan, a broker executes trades pursuant to parameters established by the director or officer when entering into the plan, without further direction from them. The director or officer may amend a Rule&#160;10b5 -1 Plan in some circumstances and may terminate a plan at any time. The directors and executive officers of the Post -Closing Company also may buy or sell additional shares outside of a Rule&#160;10b5 -1 Plan when they are not in possession of material nonpublic information subject to compliance with the terms of our insider trading policy.

 Board Composition 
 Effective upon the Closing, the Post -Closing Company Board will consist of seven, but may consist of up to nine, directors, a majority of whom will be required to qualify as an independent director under Nasdaq rules. The Post -Closing Company Board will serve staggered terms divided into three classes, Class&#160;I, Class&#160;II and Class&#160;III, with members of each class serving staggered three (3) -year terms. The term of the initial Class&#160;I members of the Post -Closing Company Board shall expire at the first annual meeting of the stockholders of SPAC following the Closing, the term of the initial Class&#160;II members of the Post -Closing Company Board shall expire at the second annual meeting of the stockholders of SPAC following the Closing and the term of the initial Class&#160;III member of the Post -Closing Company Board shall expire at the third annual meeting of the stockholders of SPAC following the Closing. 
 When considering whether directors and director nominees have the experience, qualifications, attributes and skills, taken as a whole, to enable the Post -Closing Company Board to satisfy its oversight responsibilities effectively in light of its business and structure, the Post -Closing Company Board expects to focus primarily on each person&#8217;s background and experience as reflected in the information discussed in each of the directors&#8217; individual biographies set forth above in order to provide an appropriate mix of experience and skills relevant to the size and nature of its business. 
 Director Independence 
 Under Nasdaq rules, a director is not independent unless the Board of Directors affirmatively determines that he or she does not have a direct or indirect material relationship with the Post -Closing Company or any of its subsidiaries. In addition, the director must not be precluded from qualifying as independent under the per se bars set forth by Nasdaq rules. 
 The Post -Closing Company Board will undertake a review of its composition, the composition of its committees and the independence of its directors and consider whether any director has a material relationship with the Post -Closing Company that could compromise his or her ability to exercise independent judgment in carrying out his or her responsibilities. Based upon information requested from and provided by each director concerning his or her background, employment and affiliations, including family relationships, the Post -Closing Company Board is expected to determine that &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;of the Post -Closing Company&#8217;s directors, do not have a relationship that would interfere with the exercise of independent judgment in carrying out the responsibilities of a director and that each of these directors qualifies as &#8220;independent&#8221; as that term is defined under Nasdaq rules. In making these determinations, the Post -Closing Company Board will consider the relationships that each non -employee director has with the Post -Closing Company and all other facts and circumstances the Post -Closing Company Board deemed relevant in determining their independence, including the director&#8217;s beneficial ownership of the Post -Closing Company Common Stock.

 Board Committees 
 The Post -Closing Company Board will direct the management of its business and affairs, as provided by Delaware law, and will conduct its business through meetings of the board of directors and standing committees. The Post -Closing Company will have a standing audit committee, compensation committee and nominating and corporate governance committee, each of which will operate under a written charter. 
 In addition, from time to time, special committees may be established under the direction of the Post -Closing Company Board when the Post -Closing Company Board deems it necessary or advisable to address specific issues. Following the business combination, current copies of the Post -Closing Company&#8217;s committee charters will be posted on its website, www.agilityrobotics.com as required by applicable SEC and Nasdaq rules. The information on or available through any of such website is not deemed incorporated in this proxy statement/prospectus and does not form part of this proxy statement/prospectus. 
 Audit Committee 
 Upon the consummation of the business combination, it is anticipated that the Post -Closing Company&#8217;s audit committee will consist of &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;. Prior to the Closing, the Post -Closing Company Board will have determined that each of &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;meets the independence requirements of the Sarbanes -Oxley Act, Rule&#160;10A -3 under the Exchange&#160;Act and each of the individuals meets the applicable listing standards of Nasdaq and that &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;qualifies as an audit committee financial expert within the meaning of SEC regulations and meets the financial sophistication requirements of Nasdaq rules. Each member of the Post -Closing Company&#8217;s audit committee will meet the requirements for financial literacy under the applicable Nasdaq rules. In making this determination, the Post -Closing Company Board will examine each audit committee member&#8217;s formal education and previous and current experience in financial and accounting roles. 
 The primary purpose of the audit committee is to discharge the responsibilities of the Post -Closing Company Board with respect to the Post -Closing Company&#8217;s accounting, financial, and other reporting and internal control practices and to oversee its independent registered accounting firm. Specific responsibilities of the audit committee are expected to include, among other things:

None of the Post -Closing Company&#8217;s intended executive officers currently serve, or have served during the last completed fiscal year, on the compensation committee or board of directors of any other entity that has one or more executive officers that will serve as a member of the Post -Closing Company Board or compensation committee. 
 Role of the Post-Closing Company Board in Risk Oversight/Risk Committee 
 Upon the consummation of the business combination, one of the key functions of the Post -Closing Company Board will be informed oversight of the Post -Closing Company&#8217;s risk management process. The Post -Closing Company Board does not anticipate having a standing risk management committee but rather anticipates administering this oversight function directly through the Post -Closing Company Board as a whole, as well as through various standing committees of the Post -Closing Company Board that address risks inherent in their respective areas of oversight. For example, the Post -Closing Company Board audit committee will be responsible for overseeing the management of risks 
 

 260 
 Table of Contents 

 
 associated with the Post -Closing Company&#8217;s financial reporting, operational, privacy and cybersecurity, competition, legal, regulatory, compliance and reputational matters; and the Post -Closing Company&#8217;s compensation committee will oversee the management of risks associated with our compensation policies and programs. 
 Oversight of Cybersecurity Risks 
 The Post -Closing Company will face a number of risks, including cybersecurity risks and those other risks described under the section entitled &#8220;Risk Factors&#8221; included in this proxy statement/prospectus. The audit committee will be responsible for overseeing the steps management has taken with respect to cybersecurity risk exposure. As part of this oversight, the audit committee will receive regular reports from management of the Post -Closing Company on cybersecurity risk exposure and the actions management has taken to limit, monitor or control such exposures at its regularly scheduled meetings. Management will work with third -party service providers to maintain appropriate controls. We believe this division of responsibilities is the most effective approach for addressing the Post -Closing Company&#8217;s cybersecurity risks and that the Post -Closing Company Board leadership structure supports this approach. 
 Limitation on Liability and Indemnification of Directors and Officers 
 The Proposed Charter, which will be effective upon consummation of the business combination, contains provisions that, to the fullest extent permitted by the DGCL, eliminate the personal liability of the Post -Closing Company&#8217;s directors and certain officers for monetary damages resulting from breaches of certain fiduciary duties as a director or officer. The Proposed Charter and the Post -Closing Company&#8217;s bylaws require the Post -Closing Company to indemnify and advance expenses to, to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law, its directors, officers and agents. The Post -Closing Company plans to maintain a directors&#8217; and officers&#8217; insurance policy pursuant to which the Post -Closing Company&#8217;s directors and officers are insured against liability for actions taken in their capacities as directors and officers. Finally, the Proposed Charter and the Post -Closing Company&#8217;s bylaws prohibit any retroactive changes to the rights or protections or increasing the liability of any director or officer in effect at the time of the alleged occurrence of any act or omission to act giving rise to liability or indemnification. 
 In addition, the Post -Closing Company will enter into separate indemnification agreements with the Post -Closing Company&#8217;s directors, officers, and certain employees containing provisions which are in some respects broader than the specific indemnification provisions contained in the DGCL.&#160;These agreements, among other things, require the Post -Closing Company to indemnify its directors and officers for certain expenses, including attorneys&#8217; fees, judgments, fines and settlement amounts incurred by a director or officer in any action or proceeding arising out of their services as one of the Post -Closing Company&#8217;s directors or officers or any other company or enterprise to which the person provides services at the Post -Closing Company&#8217;s request. 
 We believe these provisions in the Proposed Charter and the Post -Closing Company&#8217;s bylaws are necessary to attract and retain qualified persons as directors and officers for the Post -Closing Company following the completion of the business combination. 
 Corporate Governance Guidelines and Code of Business Conduct 
 The Post -Closing Company Board will adopt Corporate Governance Guidelines that address items such as the qualifications and responsibilities of its directors and director candidates and corporate governance policies and standards applicable to the Post -Closing Company. In addition, the Post -Closing Company Board will adopt a Code of Business Conduct and Ethics that applies to all of its employees, officers and directors, including its Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer and other executive and senior financial officers. The full text of the Post -Closing Company&#8217;s Corporate Governance Guidelines and its Code of Business Conduct and Ethics will be posted on the Corporate Governance portion of the Post -Closing Company&#8217;s website at www.agilityrobotics.com. Information contained on or accessible through the Post -Closing Company&#8217;s website is not a part of this proxy statement/prospectus, and the inclusion of the Post -Closing Company&#8217;s website address in this proxy statement/prospectus is an inactive textual reference only. The Post -Closing Company intends to make any legally required disclosures regarding amendments to, or waivers of, provisions of its code of ethics on its website rather than by filing a Current Report on Form&#160;8 -K .

 Introduction 
 On June&#160;24, 2026, CCXI entered into the Merger Agreement with Merger Sub and Agility. 
 CCXI is a blank check company formed in order to effect a merger, amalgamation, share exchange, asset acquisition, stock purchase, reorganization or other similar business combination with one or more businesses. CCXI was incorporated under the laws of the Cayman Islands on June&#160;4, 2025. 
 On December&#160;18, 2025, CCXI consummated its initial public offering of 41,400,000 CCXI public units, including 5,400,000 CCXI public units pursuant to the underwriters&#8217; full exercise of the over -allotment option. The CCXI public units were sold at an offering price of $10.00 per unit, generating gross proceeds to CCXI of $414,000,000. Simultaneously with the consummation of the CCXI IPO and the exercise of the underwriters&#8217; over -allotment option, CCXI consummated the private placement of 500,000 CCXI private placement units to the Sponsor at a price of $10.00 per unit, generating total proceeds of $5,000,000. Transaction costs amounted to $19,618,232, consisting of $3,000,000 of underwriting fees, $15,990,000 of deferred underwriting fees (of which $1,500,000 has been paid and $14,490,000 remains deferred) and $628,232 of other offering costs. 
 Agility Robotics, Inc. was organized in 2015 under the laws of the State of Delaware as a spinoff of Oregon State University, to commercialize research from the Dynamic Robotics Laboratory on bipedal locomotion. Since inception, Agility has developed several versions of a bipedal robot, referred to as Digit. Historically, Digit has been sold as a unit, deployed under robot deployment arrangements, and used for short -term customer acceleration program engagements (historically referred to as proof -of-concept or POC), with strategic partners and prospective long -term customers. These efforts are still largely considered to be research and development, and Agility is currently considered to be a development stage company. Agility is headquartered in Salem, Oregon, previously in Tangent, Oregon, with offices located in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania and San Jose, California. 
 CCXI is providing the following unaudited pro forma condensed combined financial information to aid in the analysis of the financial aspects of the business combination and other events contemplated by the Merger Agreement. The following unaudited pro forma condensed combined financial information presents the combination of the financial information of CCXI and Agility, adjusted to give effect to the business combination and other events contemplated by the Merger Agreement. The following unaudited pro forma condensed combined financial information has been prepared in accordance with Article&#160;11 of Regulation&#160;S -X . 
 The unaudited pro forma condensed combined financial statements give effect to the business combination and other events contemplated by the Merger Agreement as described in this proxy statement/prospectus. The unaudited pro forma condensed combined balance sheet as of June&#160;30, 2026 combines the historical unaudited condensed balance sheet of Agility with the historical unaudited condensed balance sheet of CCXI on a pro forma basis as if the business combination and the other events contemplated by the Merger Agreement, summarized below, had been consummated on June&#160;30, 2026. The unaudited pro forma condensed combined statement of operations for the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2026 combines the historical unaudited condensed statement of operations of Agility for the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2026 and the historical unaudited condensed statement of operations of CCXI for the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2026. The unaudited pro forma condensed combined statement of operations for the year ended December&#160;31, 2025, combines the historical audited statement of operations of Agility for the year ended December&#160;31, 2025, with the historical audited statement of operations of CCXI for the period from June&#160;4, 2025 (inception) through December&#160;31, 2025. Although CCXI was incorporated as a Cayman Islands exempted company on June&#160;4, 2025, for purposes of unaudited pro forma condensed combined statements of operation for the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2026 and the year ended December&#160;31, 2025, the business combination and other events contemplated by the Merger Agreement have been given effect as if they had been consummated as of January&#160;1, 2025. 
 The unaudited pro forma condensed combined financial statements have been prepared for informational purposes only and are not necessarily indicative of what the Post -Closing Company&#8217;s condensed financial position or results of operations actually would have been had the business combination been consummated on the dates indicated above, nor are they necessarily indicative of future results of operations. In addition, the unaudited pro&#160;forma condensed combined financial statements do not purport to project the future financial position or operating results of the Post -Closing Company.

 Description of the Business Combination 
 Pursuant to the Merger Agreement and the related agreements, and upon the terms and subject to the conditions set forth therein, CCXI will acquire Agility and Agility will become a publicly traded company through the business combination. The business combination consists of (a)&#160;the transfer of the registration of CCXI by way of continuation from the Cayman Islands to the State of Delaware (the &#8220; Domestication &#8221;), and (b)&#160;following the Domestication, the merger of Merger Sub with and into Agility, with Agility as the surviving entity and as a wholly -owned subsidiary of CCXI.&#160;Subject to the terms and conditions of the Merger Agreement, the value of the aggregate consideration to be paid to Agility stockholders, holders of Agility options and Agility convertible securities will be $2,500,000,000. At the Effective Time, each share of Agility common stock issued and outstanding immediately prior to the Effective Time (other than Excluded Shares and Dissenting Shares) will be automatically cancelled and converted into the right to receive a number of shares of Post -Closing Company common stock equal to the Exchange Ratio. The Exchange Ratio is based on the per share Equity Value (calculated in accordance with the Merger Agreement). Subject to the assumptions described herein, as of the date of this proxy statement/prospectus, shares of Post -Closing Company common stock will be issued for each issued and outstanding share of Agility common stock (after giving effect to the Conversions).

 Expected Accounting Treatment for the Transactions 
 The business combination is expected to be accounted for as a reverse recapitalization in accordance with GAAP because Agility has been determined to be the accounting acquirer under both the redemption scenarios presented. Under this method of accounting, CCXI, which is the legal acquirer, will be treated as the accounting acquiree for financial reporting purposes and Agility, which is the legal acquiree, will be treated as the accounting acquirer for financial reporting purposes. Accordingly, the consolidated assets, liabilities and results of operations of Agility will become the historical financial statements of the Post -Closing Company, and CCXI&#8217;s assets, liabilities and results of operations will be consolidated with Agility&#8217;s beginning on the acquisition date. For accounting purposes, the financial statements of the Post -Closing Company will represent a continuation of the financial statements of Agility with the business combination being treated as the equivalent of Agility issuing stock for the net assets of CCXI, accompanied by a recapitalization. The net assets of CCXI will be stated at historical costs, which are expected to approximate fair value, and no goodwill or other intangible assets will be recorded. Operations prior to the business combination will be presented as those of Agility in future reports of the Post -Closing Company. 
 Agility was determined to be the accounting acquirer under both the redemption scenarios presented based on evaluation of the following facts and circumstances: 
 &#8226; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Agility stockholders comprise a relative majority of greater than 72.7% of the voting power of the Post -Closing Company under both the redemption scenarios; 
 &#8226; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Agility will have the ability to nominate a majority of the members of the board of directors of the Post -Closing Company; 
 &#8226; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Agility&#8217;s operations prior to the business combination comprise the only ongoing operations of Post -Closing Company; 
 &#8226; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Agility&#8217;s senior management will comprise the senior management of the Post -Closing Company; 
 &#8226; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; The ongoing operations of Agility will become the operations of the Post -Closing Company; and 
 &#8226; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Agility&#8217;s headquarters will become the Post -Closing Company&#8217;s headquarters. 
 The final allocation of consideration payable to Agility equity holders will be determined upon the completion of the business combination and related events and could differ materially from the two scenarios presented. 
 Assumptions and estimates underlying the unaudited pro&#160;forma adjustments set forth in the unaudited pro&#160;forma condensed combined financial statements are described in the accompanying notes. The unaudited pro&#160;forma condensed combined financial statements have been presented for illustrative purposes only and are not necessarily indicative of the operating results and financial position that would have been achieved had the business combination occurred on the dates indicated. Further, the unaudited pro&#160;forma condensed combined financial statements do not purport to project the future operating results or financial position of CCXI following the completion of the Merger. The unaudited pro&#160;forma adjustments represent CCXI management&#8217;s estimates based on information available as of the dates of these unaudited pro&#160;forma condensed combined financial statements and are subject to change as additional information becomes available and analyses are performed.

 NOTES TO UNAUDITED PRO FORMA CONDENSED COMBINED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS 
 Note&#160;1. Basis of Pro Forma Presentation 
 The business combination will be accounted for as a reverse recapitalization in accordance with U.S.&#160;GAAP.&#160;Under this method of accounting, CCXI, who is the legal acquirer, will be treated as the accounting acquiree for financial reporting purposes and Agility, which is the legal acquiree, will be treated as the accounting acquirer for financial reporting purposes. 
 The unaudited pro&#160;forma condensed combined financial statements are prepared in accordance with Article&#160;11 of SEC Regulation&#160;S -X , as amended January&#160;1, 2021. The historical financial information of CCXI and Agility is presented in accordance with U.S.&#160;GAAP.&#160;Management has made significant estimates and assumptions in its determination of the pro&#160;forma adjustments. As the unaudited pro&#160;forma condensed combined financial information has been prepared based on these preliminary estimates, the final amounts recorded may differ materially from the information presented. The unaudited pro&#160;forma condensed combined financial information does not give effect to any anticipated synergies, operating efficiencies, tax savings or cost savings that may be associated with the business combination. 
 The pro&#160;forma adjustments reflecting the completion of the business combination and related transactions are based on currently available information and assumptions and methodologies that CCXI believes are reasonable under the circumstances. The unaudited condensed pro&#160;forma adjustments, which are described in the accompanying notes, may be revised as additional information becomes available. Therefore, it is likely that the actual adjustments will differ from the pro&#160;forma adjustments, and it is possible the difference may be material. CCXI believes that its assumptions and methodologies provide a reasonable basis for presenting all of the significant effects of the business combination and related transactions based on information available to management at the current time and that the pro&#160;forma adjustments give appropriate effect to those assumptions and are properly applied in the unaudited pro&#160;forma condensed combined financial information. 
 The unaudited pro&#160;forma condensed combined financial information is not necessarily indicative of what the actual results of operations and financial position would have been had the business combination and related transactions taken place on the dates indicated, nor are they indicative of the future consolidated results of operations or financial position of the Post -Closing Company. They should be read in conjunction with the historical financial statements and notes thereto of CCXI and Agility.

 Transaction Accounting Adjustments to Unaudited Pro Forma Condensed Combined Statement of Operations for the six&#160;months ended June&#160;30, 2026 
 (AA)&#160;Reflects the total estimated remaining transaction costs of CCXI to be incurred and expensed as a part of the business combination under both the No Redemptions and Maximum Redemptions Scenarios. Transaction costs are expensed as incurred and reflected as if incurred on January&#160;1, 2025. This is a non -recurring item. 
 (BB)&#160;Represents the elimination of investment income related to the investments held in the CCXI trust account under both the No Redemptions and Maximum Redemptions Scenarios. 
 (CC)&#160;Reflects no adjustments for the U.S. federal (and, as applicable, state and local) income tax effects of the Domestication, the Sponsor&#8217;s conversion of CCXI Class B Ordinary Shares, immediately prior to the Domestication, on a one -for-one basis, into a CCXI Class A Ordinary Share (the &#8220; Sponsor Share Conversion &#8221;), or the Merger. The lack of any such income tax adjustments assumes the intended tax treatment of the Transactions to Agility, CCXI, and Merger Sub, and the certain actions expected to be taken by each party to affect that intended treatment. Similarly, there are no adjustments for Cayman Islands income tax effects of the Transactions assuming the intended tax treatment. Additionally, this information reflects no adjustments for the U.S. federal (and, as applicable, state and local) income tax effects of any debt conversions or similar transactions which may occur or be deemed to occur for U.S. income tax purposes.  Note&#160;3. Loss per Share 
 Represents the net loss per share calculated using the historical weighted -average shares outstanding and the issuance of additional shares in connection with the business combination and related transactions, assuming the shares were outstanding since January&#160;1, 2025. In the case of shares presented as being held by Agility stockholders, the tables below assumes that Agility preferred stock outstanding as of December&#160;31, 2025 had converted to Agility common stock and that each such share of Agility common stock was exchanged for a number of shares equal to the assumed Exchange Ratio as of January&#160;1, 2025. In the case of stock options presented in the table below showing potentially dilutive instruments, the table assumes that such stock options were exchanged applying the assumed Exchange Ratio as of January&#160;1, 2025. 
 Net income loss per share was computed using the two -class method required for participating securities. The two -class method requires income available to ordinary shareholders for the period to be allocated between ordinary shares and participating securities based upon their respective rights to receive dividends as if all income for the period had been distributed. Net losses are not allocated to these participating securities as there are no contractual obligations that require participation in the Post -Closing Company&#8217;s losses. 
 As the business combination is being reflected as if it had occurred at the beginning of the earliest period presented, the calculation of weighted -average shares outstanding for basic and diluted net loss per share assumes that the shares issuable relating to the business combination and related transactions have been outstanding for the entire periods presented. When assuming the Maximum Redemptions Scenario, this calculation is adjusted to eliminate such shares for the entire period. Basic and diluted earnings per share are the same for each class of common stock because they are entitled to the same liquidation and dividend rights.

 Description of Securities 
 Unless the context otherwise requires, references in this subsection to &#8220;we,&#8221; &#8220;our&#8221; and &#8220;us&#8221; generally refer to CCXI prior to the business combination. 
 The following summary of the material terms of CCXI&#8217;s securities prior to and following the business combination is not intended to be a complete summary of the rights and preferences of such securities. 
 The terms of CCXI&#8217;s securities are currently governed by the laws of the Cayman Islands, including the Companies Act and the CCXI current articles of association. We expect to adopt the Proposed Certificate of Incorporation and Proposed Bylaws of the Post -Closing Company in connection with the consummation of the business combination, which will rename CCXI as &#8220;Agility Robotics, Inc.&#8221; As a result of the business combination, CCXI shareholders that hold CCXI Ordinary Shares and Agility stockholders that receive shares of Post -Closing Company common stock in the business combination will each become stockholders of the Post -Closing Company. 
 Because it is only a summary, this section does not contain all of the information that may be important to you. You should refer to the section entitled &#8220; Comparison of Shareholder Rights &#8221; as well as the Post -Closing Company&#8217;s Proposed Certificate of Incorporation and the Post -Closing Company&#8217;s Proposed Bylaws, which are attached to this proxy statement/prospectus as Annex&#160;B and Annex&#160;C, respectively, and to the applicable provisions of Delaware law. 
 Authorized and Outstanding Stock 
 As of the close of business on the record date for the extraordinary general meeting, there were (1) &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; CCXI Class&#160;A Ordinary Shares outstanding, (2)&#160;&#160;&#160; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Class&#160;B Ordinary Shares outstanding and (3)&#160;no CCXI preference shares outstanding. 
 All of the issued and outstanding CCXI Class&#160;B Ordinary Shares will convert into CCXI Class&#160;A Ordinary Shares on a one -for-one basis (the &#8220; initial conversion ratio &#8221;) immediately prior to the Domestication. As described under &#8220; &#8212;&#160;CCXI Capital Stock Prior to the Business Combination&#160;&#8212;&#160;CCXI Founder Shares ,&#8221; pursuant to the terms of the Sponsor Agreement, the Sponsor and the Insiders have agreed to waive any adjustment to the initial conversion ratio under the CCXI current articles of association in connection with the business combination. 
 The Proposed Certificate of Incorporation authorizes the issuance of 950,000,000 shares of capital stock, each with a par value of $0.0001, of which (1)&#160;900,000,000 shares are designated as Post -Closing Company common stock and (2)&#160;50,000,000 shares are designated as Post -Closing Company preferred stock. 
 The outstanding CCXI Ordinary Shares are, and the shares of Post -Closing Company common stock issuable in connection with the business combination will be, duly authorized, validly issued, fully paid and non -assessable . 
 Post-Closing Company Capital Stock 
 Post-Closing Company Common Stock 
 Voting rights. 
 Each holder of record of Post -Closing Company Common Stock, as such, shall have one vote for each share of Post -Closing Company Common Stock that is outstanding and held by the Post -Closing Company on all matters on which stockholders are entitled to vote generally. The holders of shares of Post -Closing Company Common Stock do not have cumulative voting rights. 
 Dividend rights. 
 Subject to applicable law and the rights, if any, of the holders of any outstanding series of Post -Closing Company Preferred Stock or any other class or series of stock, in each case having a preference over or the right to participate with Post -Closing Company Common Stock with respect to the payment of dividends and other distributions in cash, property or shares of stock of the Post -Closing Company, dividends and other distributions may be declared and paid ratably on Post -Closing Company Common Stock out of the assets of the Post -Closing Company that are legally available for this purpose at such times and in such amounts as the Post -Closing Company Board, in its discretion, shall determine. 
 

 277 
 Table of Contents 

 
 The payment of future dividends on the shares of Post -Closing Company Common Stock will depend on the financial condition of the Post -Closing Company after the completion of the business combination, and subject to the discretion of the Post -Closing Company Board. There can be no guarantee that cash dividends will be declared. The ability of the Post -Closing Company to declare dividends may be limited by the terms and conditions of other financing and other agreements entered into by the Post -Closing Company or any of its subsidiaries from time to time. 
 Rights upon liquidation. 
 In the event of dissolution, liquidation or winding up of the Post -Closing Company, after payment or provision for payment of the debts and other liabilities of the Post -Closing Company and subject to the rights, if any, of the holders of any outstanding series of Post -Closing Company Preferred Stock or any class or series of stock having a preference over or the right to participate with Post -Closing Company Common Stock with respect to the distribution of assets of the Post -Closing Company upon such dissolution, liquidation or winding up of the Post -Closing Company, the holders of Post -Closing Company Common Stock shall be entitled to receive the remaining assets of the Post -Closing Company available for distribution to its stockholders ratably in proportion to the number of shares held by them. 
 Other rights. 
 The holders of Post -Closing Company Common Stock have no pre -emptive or conversion rights or other subscription rights. There are no redemption or sinking fund provisions applicable to Post -Closing Company Common Stock. The rights, preferences and privileges of holders of Post -Closing Company Common Stock will be subject to those of the holders of any shares of Post -Closing Company Preferred Stock that the Post -Closing Company may issue in the future. 
 Agility Lock-Up Agreement 
 At the Closing, the Post -Closing Company and the Holders will enter into the A&amp;R Registration Rights Agreement, pursuant to which the Holders will agree not to, without the prior written consent of the Post -Closing Company Board, prior to the one hundred eighty (180)&#160;day anniversary of the Closing Date (i)&#160;sell, offer to sell, contract or agree to sell, hypothecate, pledge, grant any option to purchase or otherwise dispose of the Lock -Up Shares, (ii)&#160;enter into any swap or other arrangement that transfers to another, in whole or in part, any of the economic consequences of ownership of any Lock -Up Shares or (iii)&#160;publicly announce any intention to effect any of the matters described in the foregoing clauses (i)&#160;or (ii). The A&amp;R Registration Rights Agreement provides for certain permitted transfers, including but not limited to, transfers to certain affiliates or family members, transfers to satisfy tax withholding obligations in connection with the exercise of stock options or vesting of stock -based awards, and transfers in payment on a &#8220;net exercise&#8221; or &#8220;cashless&#8221; basis of stock options, subject to certain conditions. 
 Post-Closing Company Preferred Stock 
 The Proposed Certificate of Incorporation will authorize the Post -Closing Company Board to establish one or more series of Post -Closing Company Preferred Stock. Unless required by law or any stock exchange, the authorized shares of Post -Closing Company Preferred Stock will be available for issuance without further action by the holders of Post -Closing Company Common Stock. 
 The Post -Closing Company Board has the discretion to determine the powers, preferences and relative, participating, optional and other special rights, including voting rights, dividend rights, conversion rights, redemption privileges and liquidation preferences, of each series of Post -Closing Company Preferred Stock. The issuance of Post -Closing Company Preferred Stock may have the effect of delaying, deferring or preventing a change in control of the Post -Closing Company without further action by the stockholders. Additionally, the issuance of Post -Closing Company Preferred Stock may adversely affect the holders of Post -Closing Company Common Stock by restricting dividends on Post -Closing Company Common Stock, diluting the voting power of Post -Closing Company Common Stock or subordinating the liquidation rights of Post -Closing Company Common Stock. As a result of these or other factors, the issuance of Post -Closing Company Preferred Stock could have an adverse impact on the market price of the Post -Closing Company Common Stock.
