 Warrants 
 CCXI Warrants 
 In connection with the business combination and pursuant to the Domestication, each CCXI Warrant that is issued and outstanding will be converted into a CCXI Delaware Warrant to acquire a corresponding number of shares of CCXI common stock, on a one -for-one basis, pursuant to the terms of the warrant agreement and each of the then issued and outstanding CCXI Units&#160;will be cancelled and each holder of CCXI Units&#160;will be entitled to one share of CCXI common stock and one -tenth of one CCXI Delaware Warrant. No fractional CCXI Delaware Warrants will be issued upon cancellation. Upon Closing, the CCXI Delaware Warrants will be assumed by the Post -Closing Company and will become Post -Closing Company Warrants. 
 An estimated &#160;&#160;&#160; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; shares of CCXI common stock will be reserved for potential future issuance of CCXI common stock upon the exercise of the CCXI Delaware Warrants. 
 As of &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; , 2026, there were&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; CCXI Warrants outstanding, which consists of 13,800,000 CCXI public warrants and&#160;&#160;&#160; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; CCXI private placement warrants. 
 Public Warrants 
 After the Domestication, each CCXI public warrant entitles the registered holder to purchase one share of CCXI common stock at a price of $11.50 per share, subject to adjustment as discussed herein, at any time commencing 30&#160;days after the Closing Date, provided that we have an effective registration statement under the Securities Act covering the CCXI common stock issuable upon exercise of the CCXI public warrants and a current prospectus relating to them is available (or we permit holders to exercise their CCXI public warrants on a &#8220;cashless basis&#8221; under the circumstances specified in the warrant agreement) and such shares are registered, qualified or exempt from registration under the securities, or blue sky, laws of the state of residence of the holder. Pursuant to the warrant agreement, a warrantholder may exercise its CCXI public warrants only for a whole number of shares of CCXI common stock. This means that only a whole CCXI public warrant may be exercised at any given time by a warrantholder. No fractional warrants will be issued upon separation of the CCXI Units&#160;and only whole CCXI public warrants will trade. Accordingly, unless you purchase at least ten CCXI Units, you will not be able to receive or trade a whole CCXI public warrant. The CCXI public warrants will expire five&#160;years after the completion of the business combination, at 5:00&#160;p.m., New&#160;York City time, or earlier upon redemption or liquidation. 
 We will not be obligated to deliver any CCXI common stock pursuant to the exercise of a CCXI public warrant and will have no obligation to settle such warrant exercise unless a registration statement under the Securities Act with respect to the CCXI common stock underlying the CCXI public warrants is then effective and a prospectus relating thereto is current, subject to our satisfying our obligations described below with respect to registration. No CCXI public warrant will be exercisable and we will not be obligated to issue CCXI common stock upon exercise of a CCXI public warrant unless the CCXI common stock issuable upon such warrant exercise has been registered, qualified or deemed to be exempt under the securities laws of the state of residence of the registered holder of the CCXI public warrants. In the event that the conditions in the two immediately preceding sentences are not satisfied with respect to a CCXI public warrant, the holder of such CCXI public warrant will not be entitled to exercise such CCXI public warrant and such CCXI public warrant may have no value and expire without value to the holder. In no event will we be required to net cash settle any CCXI public warrant. 
 We have agreed that as soon as practicable, but in no event later than 15&#160;business days, after the closing of the business combination, we will use our commercially reasonable efforts to file with the SEC a post -effective amendment to the registration statement covering the issuance of the CCXI common stock issuable upon exercise of the CCXI public warrants. We will use our commercially reasonable efforts to cause the same to become effective and to maintain the effectiveness of such registration statement, and a current prospectus relating thereto, until the expiration or redemption of the CCXI public warrants in accordance with the provisions of the warrant agreement. Notwithstanding the above, if our shares of CCXI common stock are at the time of any exercise of a CCXI public warrant not listed on a national securities exchange such that it satisfies the definition of a &#8220;covered security&#8221; under Section&#160;18(b)(1)&#160;of the Securities Act, we may, at our option, require holders of CCXI public warrants who exercise their CCXI public warrants to do so on a &#8220;cashless basis&#8221; in accordance with Section&#160;3(a)(9)&#160;of the Securities Act and, in the event we so elect, we will not be required to file or maintain in effect a registration statement, but we will be required to use our commercially reasonable efforts to register or qualify the issuance of shares under applicable

 blue sky laws to the extent an exemption is not available. To exercise CCXI public warrants on a cashless basis, each holder would pay the exercise price by surrendering the warrants in exchange for a number of shares of CCXI common stock equal to the quotient obtained by dividing (x)&#160;the product of (i)&#160;the number of CCXI common stock underlying the CCXI public warrants, and (ii)&#160;the excess of the &#8220;fair market value&#8221; (defined below) over the exercise price of the warrants by (y)&#160;such fair market value. Solely for the purposes of the preceding sentence, &#8220;fair market value&#8221; shall mean the 10 -day average trading price as of the date on which the notice of exercise is received by the warrant agent. 
 Redemption of warrants for cash when the price per share of CCXI common stock equals or exceeds $18.00 
 Beginning 30&#160;days after completion of the business combination, we may redeem the outstanding public warrants for cash: 
 &#8226; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; in whole and not in part; 
 &#8226; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; at a price of $0.01 per warrant; 
 &#8226; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; upon not less than 30&#160;days&#8217; prior written notice of redemption (the &#8220; 30 -day redemption period &#8221;); and 
 &#8226; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; if, and only if, the last reported sale price of the CCXI common stock equals or exceeds $18.00 per share (as adjusted for share subdivisions, share dividends, reorganizations, recapitalizations and the like) for any 20&#160;trading days within a 30&#160;trading day period ending on the third&#160;trading day prior to the date on which we send the notice of redemption to the warrantholders. We will not redeem the CCXI public warrants as described above unless a registration statement under the Securities Act covering the CCXI common stock issuable upon exercise of the warrants is effective and a current prospectus relating to those shares of CCXI common stock is available throughout such 30&#160;trading day period and the 30&#160;day redemption period. 
 If and when the CCXI public warrants become redeemable by us, we may exercise our redemption right even if we are unable to register or qualify the underlying securities for sale under all applicable state securities laws. 
 We have established the last of the redemption criteria discussed above to prevent a redemption call unless there is at the time of the call a significant premium to the warrant exercise price. If the foregoing conditions are satisfied and we issue a notice of redemption of the CCXI public warrants, each warrantholder will be entitled to exercise its warrant prior to the scheduled redemption date. However, the price of the CCXI common stock may fall below the $18.00 redemption trigger price (as adjusted for share subdivisions, share dividends, reorganizations, recapitalizations and the like) as well as the $11.50 (for whole shares) warrant exercise price after the redemption notice is issued. 
 Redemption Procedures 
 A holder of a CCXI public warrant may notify us in writing in the event it elects to be subject to a requirement that such holder will not have the right to exercise such CCXI public warrant, to the extent that after giving effect to such exercise, such person (together with such person&#8217;s affiliates), to the warrant agent&#8217;s actual knowledge, would beneficially own in excess of 9.8% (or such other amount as a holder may specify) of the CCXI common stock outstanding immediately after giving effect to such exercise. 
 Anti-Dilution Adjustments 
 If the number of outstanding shares of CCXI common stock is increased by a share dividend payable in CCXI common stock, or by a subdivision of CCXI common stock or other similar event, then, on the effective date of such share dividend, subdivision or similar event, the number of shares of CCXI common stock issuable on exercise of each CCXI public warrant will be increased in proportion to such increase in the outstanding shares of CCXI common stock. A rights offering to holders of CCXI common stock entitling holders to purchase shares of CCXI common stock at a price less than the fair market value will be deemed a share dividend of a number of CCXI common stock equal to the product of (i)&#160;the number of shares of CCXI common stock actually sold in such rights offering (or issuable under any other equity securities sold in such rights offering that are convertible into or exercisable for CCXI common stock) multiplied by (ii)&#160;one (1)&#160;minus the quotient of (x)&#160;the price per CCXI common stock paid in such rights offering divided by (y)&#160;the fair market value. For these purposes (i)&#160;if the rights offering is for securities convertible into or exercisable for CCXI common stock, in determining the price payable for CCXI common stock, there will be taken into account any consideration received for such rights, as well as any additional amount payable upon exercise or 
 

 280 
 Table of Contents 

 
 conversion, (ii)&#160;10 -day average closing price means, as of any date, the average last reported sale price of the CCXI common stock as reported during the ten (10)&#160;trading&#160;day period ending on the&#160;trading day prior to such date and (iii)&#160;fair market value means the 10 -day average closing price the first date on which the CCXI common stock trade on the applicable exchange or in the applicable market, regular way, without the right to receive such rights. 
 In addition, if we, at any time while the CCXI public warrants are outstanding and unexpired, pay a dividend or make a distribution in cash, securities or other assets to the holders of CCXI common stock on account of such shares of CCXI common stock (or other shares into which the warrants are convertible), other than (a)&#160;as described shares in connection with a proposed initial business combination, or (b)&#160;in connection with the redemption of our CCXI Ordinary Shares upon our failure to complete the business combination, then the warrant exercise price will be decreased, effective immediately after the effective date of such event, by the amount of cash and/or the fair market value of any securities or other assets paid on each share of CCXI common stock in respect of such event. 
 If the number of outstanding shares of CCXI common stock is decreased by a consolidation, combination, or reclassification of CCXI common stock or other similar event, then, on the effective date of such consolidation, combination, reclassification or similar event, the number of CCXI common stock issuable on exercise of each warrant will be decreased in proportion to such decrease in outstanding shares of CCXI common stock. 
 Whenever the number of shares of CCXI common stock purchasable upon the exercise of the CCXI public warrants is adjusted, as described above, the warrant exercise price will be adjusted by multiplying the warrant exercise price immediately prior to such adjustment by a fraction (x)&#160;the numerator of which will be the number of shares of CCXI common stock purchasable upon the exercise of the CCXI public warrants immediately prior to such adjustment, and (y)&#160;the denominator of which will be the number of shares of CCXI common stock so purchasable immediately thereafter. The warrant agreement provides that no adjustment to the number of the shares of CCXI common stock issuable upon exercise of a CCXI public warrant will be required until cumulative adjustments amount to 1% or more of the number of shares of CCXI common stock issuable upon exercise of a CCXI public warrant as last adjusted. Any such adjustments that are not made will be carried forward and taken into account in any subsequent adjustment. All such carried forward adjustments will be made (i)&#160;in connection with any subsequent adjustment that (taken together with such carried forward adjustments) would result in a change of at least 1% in the number of shares of CCXI common stock issuable upon exercise of a CCXI public warrant and (ii)&#160;on the exercise date of any CCXI public warrant. 
 In the case of any reclassification or reorganization of the outstanding shares of CCXI common stock (other than those described above or that solely affects the par value of such CCXI common stock), or in the case of any merger or consolidation of us with or into another entity in which any &#8220;person&#8221; or &#8220;group&#8221; (as such terms are used in Section&#160;13(d)&#160;and 14(d)&#160;of the Exchange&#160;Act) acquires more than 50% of the voting power of the securities, or in the case of any sale or conveyance to another corporation or entity of the assets or other property of us as an entirety or substantially as an entirety, the holders of the CCXI public warrants will thereafter have the right to purchase and receive, upon the basis and upon the terms and conditions specified in the warrants and in lieu of our CCXI common stock immediately theretofore purchasable and receivable upon the exercise of the rights represented thereby, the kind and amount of shares or other securities or property (including cash) receivable upon such reclassification, reorganization, merger or consolidation, or any such sale or transfer, that the holder of the CCXI public warrants would have received if such holder had exercised their warrants immediately prior to such event. 
 The CCXI public warrants have been issued in registered form under a warrant agreement between Continental Stock Transfer&#160;&amp; Trust Company, as warrant agent, and us. You should review a copy of the warrant agreement, which is as an exhibit to this proxy statement/prospectus, for a complete description of the terms and conditions applicable to the CCXI public warrants. The warrant agreement provides that the terms of the CCXI public warrants may be amended without the consent of any holder to cure any ambiguity or correct any mistake, including to conform the provisions of the warrant agreement to the description of the terms of the CCXI public warrants and the warrant agreement set forth in this proxy statement/prospectus, but requires the approval by the holders of at least 50% of the then outstanding CCXI public warrants to make generally any change that adversely affects the interests of the registered holders of CCXI public warrants. The CCXI public warrants may be exercised upon surrender of the CCXI public warrant certificate on or prior to the expiration date at the offices of the warrant agent, with the exercise form on the reverse side of the warrant certificate completed and executed as indicated, accompanied by full payment of the exercise price (or on a &#8220;cashless basis,&#8221; if applicable), by certified or official bank check payable to us, for the number of CCXI public warrants being exercised. The warrantholders do not have the rights or privileges of holders of shares

 of CCXI common stock or any voting rights until they exercise their CCXI public warrants and receive shares of CCXI common stock. After the issuance of shares of CCXI common stock upon exercise of the CCXI public warrants, each holder will be entitled to one (1)&#160;vote for each share held of record on all matters to be voted on by shareholders. 
 We have agreed that, subject to applicable law, any action, proceeding or claim against us arising out of or relating in any way to the warrant agreement will be brought and enforced in the courts of the State of New&#160;York located in the County of New&#160;York or the United&#160;States District Court for the Southern District of New&#160;York, and we irrevocably submit to such jurisdiction, which jurisdiction will be the exclusive forum for any such action, proceeding or claim.  Private Placement Warrants 
 The CCXI private placement warrants are non -redeemable . The CCXI private placement warrants may also be exercised on a &#8220;cashless basis,&#8221; but in no event will we be required to net cash settle any CCXI private placement warrant. The CCXI private placement warrants will not expire except upon liquidation. Otherwise, the CCXI private placement warrants have terms and provisions that are identical to those of the CCXI public warrants, including as to exercise price, exercisability and exercise period. 
 If holders of the CCXI private placement warrants elect to exercise them on a &#8220;cashless basis,&#8221; they would pay the exercise price by surrendering the CCXI private placement warrants in exchange for a number of shares of CCXI common stock equal to the quotient obtained by dividing (x)&#160;the product of (A)&#160;the number of shares of CCXI common stock underlying the CCXI private placement warrants, and (B)&#160;the excess of the &#8220;10 -day average closing price&#8221; (as defined below), as of the date prior to the date on which notice of exercise is sent or given to the warrant agent less the warrant price by (y)&#160;such 10 -day average closing price. The &#8220;10 -day average closing price&#8221; shall mean, as of any date, the average last reported sale price of the CCXI common stock as reported during the 10&#160;trading day period ending on the&#160;trading day prior to such date. If the holders of CCXI private placement warrants are affiliated with us, their ability to sell our securities in the open market will be significantly limited. We have policies in place that prohibit insiders from selling our securities except during specific periods of time. Even during such periods of time when insiders are permitted to sell our securities, an insider cannot trade in our securities if he or she is in possession of material non -public information. Accordingly, unlike public shareholders who could sell CCXI common stock issuable upon exercise of the CCXI public warrants freely in the open market to fund their cash exercise price, the insiders could be significantly restricted from doing so. As a result, we believe that allowing the holders to exercise such warrants on a &#8220;cashless basis&#8221; is appropriate. 
 Neither the CCXI private placement warrants nor the CCXI public warrants contain any provisions that are dependent upon the characteristics of the holder of the warrant.

 Anti-Takeover Effects of Certain Provisions of Delaware Law, the Proposed Certificate of Incorporation and the Proposed Bylaws 
 The Proposed Charter does not provide for cumulative voting in the election of directors. The Post -Closing Company Board is empowered to elect a director to fill a vacancy created by the expansion of the Post -Closing Company Board or the resignation, death, or removal of a director in certain circumstances. 
 Authorized Post -Closing Company Common Stock and Post -Closing Company Preferred Stock are available for future issuances without stockholder approval and could be utilized for a variety of corporate purposes, including future offerings to raise additional capital, acquisitions and employee benefit plans. The existence of authorized but unissued and unreserved Post -Closing Company Common Stock and Post -Closing Company Preferred Stock could render more difficult or discourage an attempt to obtain control of us by means of a proxy contest, tender offer, merger or otherwise. 
 Exclusive Forum 
 The Proposed Charter will provide that, unless the Post -Closing Company consents in writing to the selection of an alternative forum, (a)&#160;the Chancery Court (or, in the event that the Chancery Court does not have jurisdiction, the federal district court for the District of Delaware or other state courts of the State of Delaware) will be the sole and exclusive forum for (1)&#160;any derivative action, suit or proceeding brought on behalf of the Post -Closing Company, (2)&#160;any action, suit or proceeding asserting a claim of breach of a fiduciary duty owed by any director or officer of the Post -Closing Company to the Post -Closing Company or to the Post -Closing Company&#8217;s stockholders, (3)&#160;any action, suit or proceeding arising pursuant to any provision of the DGCL or Proposed Charter or the Proposed Bylaws (as either may be amended from time to time) or (4)&#160;any action, suit or proceeding asserting a claim against the Post -Closing Company governed by the internal affairs doctrine; and (b)&#160;subject to the provisions of the Proposed Charter, the federal district courts of the United&#160;States of America shall be the exclusive forum for the resolution of any complaint asserting a cause or causes of action arising under the Securities Act, including all causes of action asserted against any defendant to such complaint. If any action the subject matter of which is within the scope of clause (a)&#160;of the immediately preceding sentence is filed in a court other than the courts in the State of Delaware (a &#8220; Foreign Action &#8221;) in the name of any stockholder, such stockholder shall be deemed to have consented to (x)&#160;the personal jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in the State of Delaware in connection with any action brought in any such court to enforce the provisions of clause (a)&#160;of the immediately preceding sentence and (y)&#160;having service of process made upon such stockholder in any such action by service upon such stockholder&#8217;s counsel in the Foreign Action as agent for such stockholder. 
 Although the Post -Closing Company believes this provision benefits the Post -Closing Company by providing increased consistency in the application of Delaware law in the types of lawsuits to which it applies, a court may determine that this provision is unenforceable, and to the extent it is enforceable, the provision may have the effect of discouraging lawsuits against the Post -Closing Company&#8217;s directors and officers, although the Post -Closing Company&#8217;s stockholders will not be deemed to have waived the Post -Closing Company&#8217;s compliance with federal securities laws and the rules and regulations thereunder.

 Comparison of Shareholder Rights 
 Unless the context otherwise requires, references in this subsection to &#8220;we,&#8221; &#8220;our&#8221; and &#8220;us&#8221; generally refer to CCXI prior to the business combination. 
 CCXI is incorporated under the laws of the Cayman Islands and the rights of CCXI shareholders are governed by the laws of the Cayman Islands, including the Cayman Act and the CCXI current articles of association. Agility is incorporated under the laws of the State of Delaware, and the rights of Agility stockholders are governed by the laws of the State of Delaware, including the DGCL and Agility&#8217;s current certificate of incorporation. As a result of the Transactions, CCXI&#8217;s current shareholders who will hold shares of CCXI common stock and Agility&#8217;s stockholders who receive shares of CCXI common stock in the business combination will each become stockholders in the Post -Closing Company. The Post -Closing Company will be incorporated under the laws of the State of Delaware and the rights of Post -Closing Company stockholders will be governed by the laws of the State of Delaware, including the DGCL, the Proposed Certificate of Incorporation and the Proposed Bylaws. Thus, following the business combination and the Domestication, the rights of stockholders of the Post -Closing Company will be governed by Delaware law, including the DGCL, rather than by the laws of the Cayman Islands. Certain differences exist between the DGCL and the Companies Act that will alter certain of the rights of shareholders of CCXI and the stockholders of Agility and affect the powers of the Post -Closing Company Board and management. 
 This section describes the material differences among the rights of Agility stockholders under Agility&#8217;s current certificate of incorporation, CCXI shareholders under the CCXI current articles of association and the proposed rights of the Post -Closing Company&#8217;s stockholders under the Proposed Certificate of Incorporation and the Proposed Bylaws, which are attached to this proxy statement/prospectus as Annex&#160;B and Annex&#160;C, respectively. The summary set forth below is not intended to be complete or to provide a comprehensive discussion of each company&#8217;s governing documents and is qualified in its entirety by reference to the full text of those documents, as well as the relevant provisions of the Companies Act and the DGCL.

 Anti-Takeover Provisions 
 

 
 

 Agility 
 
 &#160; 
 
 CCXI 
 
 &#160; 
 
 Post-Closing Company 
 
 
 
 
 Agility is subject to Section&#160;203 of the DGCL. 
 Under Agility&#8217;s current certificate of incorporation, at any time when at least 3,898,606 shares of Preferred Stock are outstanding, Agility may not enter into any merger or consolidation or amend its organizational documents, without the written consent or affirmative vote of the holders of at least a majority of the then-outstanding shares of Preferred Stock (voting together as a single class on an as-converted to Common Stock basis). 
 
 &#160; 
 
 The CCXI current articles of association provide for a classified board. In addition, prior to the closing of CCXI&#8217;s initial business combination, only holders of CCXI Class&#160;B Ordinary Shares have the right to appoint and remove directors. 
 CCXI&#8217;s authorized but unissued ordinary shares and preference shares are available for future issuances generally without shareholder approval and could be utilized for a variety of corporate purposes, including future offerings to raise additional capital, acquisitions and employee benefit plans. The existence of authorized but unissued and unreserved ordinary shares and preference shares could render more difficult or discourage an attempt to obtain control of us by means of a proxy contest, tender offer, merger or otherwise. 
 
 &#160; 
 
 The Proposed Certificate of Incorporation also provides for a classified board. 
 The Post -Closing Company is subject to Section&#160;203 of the DGCL. 
 The Proposed Certificate of Incorporation authorizes the Post -Closing Company Board to issue, without action by stockholders, up to 50,000,000 shares of Post -Closing Company preferred stock. 
 The Proposed Certificate of Incorporation and the Proposed Bylaws will authorize a majority of the Post -Closing Company Board then in office to fill vacancies on the board and newly -created directorships resulting from an increase in the authorized number of directors. In addition, the number of directors constituting the Post -Closing Company Board will be set only by resolution adopted by a majority vote of the Post -Closing Company Board. For more information about the anti -takeover provisions in the Post -Closing Company&#8217;s governing documents, please see the section entitled, &#8220; Description of Securities&#160;&#8212;&#160;Anti takeover effects of Delaware law and the Post -Closing Company&#8217;s Certificate of Incorporation and Post -Closing Company&#8217;s Bylaws &#8221;

 BENEFICIAL OWNERSHIP OF SECURITIES 
 The following table sets forth information known to CCXI regarding (1)&#160;the beneficial ownership of CCXI Ordinary Shares as of &#160;&#160;&#160; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; , 2026 (pre -business combination) and (2)&#160;the expected beneficial ownership following the Closing (post -business combination) of Post -Closing Company common stock (assuming a No Redemption Scenario and a Maximum Redemptions Scenario as described below) by: 
 &#8226; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; each of CCXI&#8217;s current executive officers and directors, and all executive officers and directors of CCXI as a group, in each case pre -business combination; 
 &#8226; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; each person who will become a named executive officer or director of the Post -Closing Company, and all executive officers and directors of the Post -Closing Company as a group, in each case post -business combination; 
 &#8226; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; each person who is known to be the beneficial owner of more than five percent of (i)&#160;CCXI Class&#160;A Ordinary Shares and (ii)&#160;CCXI Class&#160;B Ordinary Shares pre -business combination; and 
 &#8226; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; each person who is expected to be the beneficial owner of more than five percent of the Post -Closing Company common stock post -business combination. 
 Beneficial ownership is determined according to the rules of the SEC, which generally provide that a person has beneficial ownership of a security if they possess sole or shared voting or investment power over that security, including options and warrants that are currently exercisable or exercisable within 60&#160;days. Unless otherwise indicated, CCXI believes that all persons named in the table below have sole voting and investment power with respect to the voting securities beneficially owned by them. 
 The beneficial ownership of CCXI Ordinary Shares pre -business combination is based on&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;CCXI Class&#160;A Ordinary Shares and&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;CCXI Class&#160;B Ordinary Shares issued and outstanding as of&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;, 2026. 
 The expected beneficial ownership of the Post -Closing Company common stock post -business combination assumes two scenarios: (1)&#160;no CCXI public shares are redeemed, and (2)&#160;the maximum number of&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;CCXI public shares are redeemed. Based on the foregoing assumptions, and in each case including the&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;shares of CCXI common stock to be issued in connection with the PIPE Investment, it is estimated that there would be&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;shares of Agility common stock issued and outstanding in the No Redemption Scenario and&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;shares of Agility common stock issued and outstanding in the Maximum Redemptions Scenario.

 Certain Relationships and Related Person Transactions 
 References in this subsection to &#8220;Agility,&#8221; &#8220;the Company,&#8221; &#8220;we,&#8221; &#8220;us&#8221; or &#8220;our&#8221; refer to the business of Agility and its subsidiaries prior to the consummation of the business combination, which will be the business of the Post -Closing Company and its subsidiaries following the business combination. 
 CCXI Related Person Transactions 
 In June&#160;2025, the Sponsor acquired an aggregate of 8,625,000 CCXI Founder Shares, for approximately $0.003 per share. In November&#160;2025, CCXI, through a share capitalization, issued the Sponsor an additional 2,875,000 CCXI Founder Shares. In December&#160;2025, CCXI, through a share capitalization, issued the Sponsor an additional 2,300,000 CCXI Founder Shares, for which the Sponsor now holds 13,800,000 CCXI Founder Shares in the aggregate. The Sponsor agreed to forfeit up to an aggregate of 1,800,000 CCXI Founder Shares to the extent that the over -allotment option was not exercised in full by the underwriters so that the number of CCXI Founder Shares issued was determined based on the expectation that such CCXI Founder Shares would represent 25% of the outstanding CCXI Ordinary Shares upon completion of the CCXI IPO (not including the CCXI Class&#160;A Ordinary Shares underlying the CCXI private placement units). The CCXI Founder Shares (including the CCXI Class&#160;A Ordinary Shares issuable upon exercise thereof) may not, subject to certain limited exceptions, be transferred, assigned or sold by the holder. As a result of the full exercise of the over -allotment option by the underwriter, the 1,800,000 CCXI Founder Shares are no longer subject to forfeiture. 
 In December&#160;2025, the Sponsor purchased an aggregate of 500,000 CCXI private placement units, at a price of $10.00 per unit, for an aggregate purchase price of $5,000,000, in the private placement in connection with the CCXI IPO.&#160;Each CCXI private placement warrant contained in the CCXI private placement units is exercisable to purchase one whole CCXI Class&#160;A Ordinary Share at a price of $11.50 per share. The CCXI private placement warrants will become exercisable 30&#160;days after the Closing Date. The CCXI private placement warrants (including the CCXI Class&#160;A Ordinary Shares issuable upon exercise thereof) may not, subject to certain limited exceptions, be transferred, assigned or sold by the holder until 30&#160;days after the Closing Date; however, if the business combination is consummated, each Sponsor Signatory holding the CCXI private placement warrants has agreed to the Sponsor Lockup. See the section entitled &#8220; Proposal&#160;No.&#160;1 &#8212;&#160;The Business Combination Proposal&#160;&#8212;&#160;Certain Agreements Related to the Business Combination&#160;&#8212;&#160;Sponsor Agreement. &#8221; The CCXI private placement warrants are non -redeemable and exercisable for cash or on a &#8220;cashless basis.&#8221; The CCXI private placement warrants do not expire except upon liquidation. 
 In December&#160;2025, CCXI agreed to reimburse M.&#160;Klein Associates, Inc., the managing member of the Sponsor, through its affiliate the Klein Group, LLC, an amount equal to $30,000 per month for office space, utilities and secretarial and administrative support made available to us. In addition, CCXI has agreed, pursuant to an administrative services and indemnification agreement with the managing member of the Sponsor, that it will indemnify the Sponsor from any claims arising out of or relating to the CCXI IPO, or its operations or conduct of its business (including the business combination) or any claims against CCXI alleging any expressed or implied management or endorsement by them of any of its activities or any express or implied association between the Sponsor and CCXI, which agreement provides that the indemnified parties cannot access the funds held in CCXI&#8217;s trust account. Upon completion of the business combination or CCXI&#8217;s liquidation, the obligation to continue paying these monthly fees will be terminated and CCXI will cease paying these monthly fees. 
 Michael Klein, a director of CCXI, and the controlling shareholder of M.&#160;Klein Associates, Inc., which is the managing member of the Sponsor, may be deemed to beneficially own the securities of CCXI owned by Sponsor. For more information about CCXI&#8217;s officers&#8217; and directors&#8217; economic interests in the Transactions, see the section entitled &#8220; Beneficial Ownership of Securities .&#8221; 
 Prior to or in connection with the completion of the business combination, there may be payment by the Company to the Sponsor, its officers or directors, or CCXI&#8217;s or their affiliates, of a finder&#8217;s fee, advisory fee, consulting fee or success fee for any services they render in order to effectuate the completion of the business combination, which, if made prior to the completion of the initial business combination, will be paid from (1)&#160;funds held outside the trust account or (2)&#160;permitted withdrawals. 
 The Sponsor, its executive officers and directors, or any of their respective affiliates, are entitled to reimbursement for any out -of-pocket expenses incurred in connection with activities on CCXI&#8217;s behalf such as identifying potential target businesses and performing due diligence on suitable business combinations. CCXI&#8217;s audit committee reviews

 on a quarterly basis all payments that were made to the Sponsor, its officers or directors or CCXI&#8217;s or their affiliates. Any such payments prior to an initial business combination are made from funds held outside the trust account, including permitted withdrawals.

 In June&#160;2025, CCXI and the Sponsor entered into a loan agreement, whereby the Sponsor agreed to loan CCXI an aggregate of up to $600,000 to cover expenses related to the CCXI IPO pursuant to the IPO Promissory Note. This loan was non -interest bearing and payable on the earlier of December&#160;31, 2026, or the date on which the Company consummated the CCXI IPO.&#160;As of June 30, 2026 and December&#160;31, 2025, there was $0 outstanding under the IPO Promissory Note. The Company repaid the borrowings in full at the closing of the CCXI IPO.&#160;Borrowings under the IPO Promissory Note are no longer available. 
 In addition, in order to fund working capital deficiencies or finance transaction costs in connection with an intended business combination, the Sponsor, CCXI or their respective affiliates may, but are not obligated to, loan CCXI funds as may be required. If CCXI completes the business combination, CCXI would repay the Working Capital Loans. In the event that the business combination does not close, CCXI may use a portion of the working capital held outside the trust account to repay the Working Capital Loans but no proceeds from the trust account would be used for such repayment. Initially, up to $1,500,000 of such Working Capital Loans may be converted into units of the Post -Closing Company at a price of $10.00 per unit, at the option of the lender. On August 7, 2026, in connection with the issuance of the August 2026 Note, the CCXI Board approved an additional $1,500,000 of Working Capital Loans that may be convertible into units of the Post -Closing Company at a price of $10.00 per unit at the option of the lender. Except as set forth above, the terms of the Working Capital Loans by CCXI&#8217;s officers and directors, if any, have not been determined and no written agreements exist with respect to the Working Capital Loans. Prior to the completion of the business combination, CCXI does not expect to seek loans from parties other than the Sponsor or an affiliate of the Sponsor as CCXI does not believe third parties will be willing to loan such funds and provide a waiver against any and all rights to seek access to funds in the trust account. As of June 30, 2026 and December&#160;31, 2025, CCXI had no borrowings under the Working Capital Loans. On July&#160;2, 2026, we issued an unsecured promissory note in the aggregate principal amount of up to $1,500,000 to the Sponsor (the &#8220; July 2026 Note &#8221;), for working capital needs. As of the date of this proxy statement/prospectus, we have borrowed the full $1,500,000 available under the July 2026 Note. On August 7, 2026, CCXI issued an additional unsecured promissory note in the aggregate principal amount of up to $1,500,000 to the Sponsor (the &#8220; August 2026 Note &#8221;), for working capital needs. The August 2026 Note may be convertible into units of the Post -Closing Company at a price of $10.00 per unit at the option of the lender. As of the date of this proxy statement/prospectus, CCXI has borrowed $750,000 under the August 2026 Note. 
 CCXI has agreed to indemnify the Sponsor and its members (present and former), managers and affiliates and their respective present and former officers and directors to the fullest extent permitted under applicable law from any claims made by CCXI or a third party in respect of any investment opportunities sourced by them or any liability arising with respect to their activities in connection with CCXI&#8217;s affairs, to the extent that such indemnification, hold harmless and exoneration obligations with respect to such matters are not expressly covered by a separate written agreement between CCXI and any such party. Such indemnity will provide that the indemnified parties cannot access the funds held in the trust account. 
 After the business combination, members of CCXI&#8217;s management team who remain with CCXI may be paid consulting, management or other fees from the combined company with any and all amounts being fully disclosed to CCXI&#8217;s shareholders, to the extent then known, in this proxy statement/prospectus or other proxy solicitation materials (as applicable) furnished to CCXI&#8217;s shareholders. It is unlikely the amount of such compensation is fully known at the time of distribution of this proxy statement/prospectus, or will be fully known at the time of a general meeting held to consider the business combination, as it will be up to the directors of the Post -Closing Company to determine executive and director compensation.

 Series&#160;C-3 Financing 
 On June&#160;25, 2025, Agility entered into a Series&#160;C -3 Preferred Stock Purchase Agreement (the &#8220; Purchase Agreement &#8221;), providing for the sale and issuance of up to 6,047,295 shares of Series&#160;C -3 Preferred Stock at a cash purchase price of $66.1452 per share. The Series&#160;C -3 Financing was conducted across multiple closings beginning with the initial closing on June&#160;25, 2025 and continuing through multiple subsequent through March&#160;30, 2026. The term sheet for the Series&#160;C -3 Financing contemplated total new cash proceeds of up to $400.0&#160;million. 
 DCVC&#160;VI, L.P. purchased shares of Series&#160;C -3 Preferred Stock for an aggregate purchase price of approximately $14.5&#160;million in the Series&#160;C -3 Financing. 
 Amended and Restated Investors&#8217; Rights Agreement: &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; On June&#160;25, 2025, Agility entered into an Amended and Restated Investors&#8217; Rights Agreement (the &#8220; Investor Rights Agreement &#8221;) with certain significant stockholders, including Amazon.com NV Investment Holdings LLC, DCVC&#160;V, L.P., DCVC&#160;VI, L.P., Playground Ventures&#160;II, L.P., and Playground Acquire, L.P., among others. The Investors&#8217; Rights Agreement provides certain investors with customary demand and piggyback registration rights for &#8220;Registrable Securities,&#8221; information and inspection rights, confidentiality obligations and a right of first offer on future issuances of &#8220;New Securities&#8221; for &#8220;Major Investors&#8221; (defined as any Investor that, individually or together with such Investor&#8217;s Affiliates, holds at least 500,000 shares of Registrable Securities as adjusted for stock splits, dividends, combinations, or other recapitalizations). The Investor Rights Agreement also provides board observer rights for Playground, DCVC, and WP Global, entitling each to invite a representative to attend all meetings of the Board of Directors in a nonvoting observer capacity so long as such investor owns shares of Preferred Stock (or Common Stock issued upon conversion thereof), subject to customary limitations regarding attorney -client privilege, trade secrets, and conflicts of interest. 
 Amended and Restated Voting Agreement: &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; On June&#160;25, 2025, Agility entered into an Amended and Restated Voting Agreement (the &#8220; Voting Agreement &#8221;) with certain investors and key holders, including DCVC&#160;V, L.P., DCVC&#160;VI, L.P., Playground Ventures&#160;II, L.P., and Playground Acquire, L.P.&#160;The Voting Agreement provides that the Board shall consist of six directors. The Voting Agreement provides certain preferred and common holders with rights to elect specified directors and includes customary provisions governing the voting and transfer of shares. It also contains drag -along provisions that, upon requisite approvals (including Board approval and specified stockholder majorities), require stockholders to support a &#8220;Sale of the Company,&#8221; subject to stated conditions.

 Right of First Refusal and Co -Sale Agreement:&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; On June&#160;25, 2025, Agility entered into an Amended and Restated Right of First Refusal and Co -Sale Agreement (the &#8220; ROFR Agreement &#8221; and, together with the Voting Agreement and the Investor Rights Agreement, the &#8220; Series&#160;C Agreements &#8221;) with certain investors and key holders, including DCVC&#160;V, L.P., DCVC&#160;VI, L.P., Playground Ventures&#160;II, L.P., and Playground Acquire, L.P.&#160;The ROFR Agreement grants the Company a right of first refusal and provides secondary purchase and co sale rights to the certain investors over transfers by &#8220;Key Holders,&#8221; including founders and certain executives.  The Company Board reviewed the Series&#160;C -3 Agreements and the rights described above and determined that they were negotiated at arm&#8217;s length with third -party investors and are customary for private venture -backed companies at the Company&#8217;s stage. The Board also considered the interests of directors affiliated with investor funds party to the Series&#160;C -3 Agreements when approving these transactions.

 Indemnification Agreements 
 In connection with the Closing, the Post -Closing Company intends to enter into indemnification agreements with each of its directors and executive officers that may be broader than the specific indemnification provisions contained in the DGCL.&#160;These indemnification agreements will require the Post -Closing Company, among other things, to indemnify its directors and executive officers against liabilities that may arise by reason of their status or service to the fullest extent permitted by law. These indemnification agreements will also require the Post -Closing Company to advance all expenses incurred by the directors and executive officers in investigating or defending any such action, suit, or proceeding to the fullest extent permitted by law. The Proposed Bylaws will also empower the Post -Closing Company to purchase insurance on behalf of any person whom the Post -Closing Company is required or permitted to indemnify. For additional information related to the Post -Closing Company&#8217;s indemnification obligations in respect of its directors and officers, see the section entitled &#8220; Board of Directors and Management After the Business Combination&#160;&#8212;&#160;Limitations on Liability and Indemnification of Officers and Directors. &#8221; We believe that the indemnification provisions in the Proposed Certificate of Incorporation and the Proposed Bylaws, liability insurance and any indemnification agreements that may be entered into are necessary to attract and retain talented and experienced directors and officers. 
 Policies and Procedures for Related Person Transactions 
 The Post -Closing Company intends to adopt a related person transactions policy setting forth the policies and procedures for the identification, review and approval or ratification of related person transactions. This policy will cover, with certain exceptions set forth in Item&#160;404 of Regulation&#160;S -K under the Securities Act, any transaction, arrangement, or relationship, or any series of similar transactions, arrangements or relationships, in which we and a related person were or will be participants and the amount involved exceeds $120,000, including purchases of goods or services by or from the related person or entities in which the related person has a material interest, indebtedness, and guarantees of indebtedness. In reviewing and approving any such transactions, the Post -Closing Company&#8217;s audit committee will consider all relevant facts and circumstances as appropriate, such as the purpose of the transaction, the availability of other sources of comparable offerings or services, whether the transaction is on terms comparable to those that could be obtained in an arm&#8217;s length transaction, management&#8217;s recommendation with respect to the proposed related person transaction, and the extent of the related person&#8217;s interest in the transaction.

 Securities Act Restrictions on Resale of CCXI&#8217;S Securities 
 Unless the context otherwise requires, references in this subsection to &#8220;we,&#8221; &#8220;our&#8221; and &#8220;us&#8221; generally refer to CCXI prior to the business combination. 
 In general, Rule&#160;144 of the Securities Act (&#8220; Rule&#160;144 &#8221;) permits the resale of restricted securities without registration under the Securities Act if certain conditions are met. Rule&#160;144 is not available for the resale of restricted securities initially issued by shell companies (other than business combination -related shell companies) or issuers that have been at any time previously a shell company, including us. However, Rule&#160;144 also includes an important exception to this prohibition if the following conditions are met at the time of such resale: 
 &#8226; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; the issuer of the securities that was formerly a shell company has ceased to be a shell company; 
 &#8226; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; the issuer of the securities is subject to the reporting requirements of Section&#160;13 or 15(d)&#160;of the Exchange&#160;Act; 
 &#8226; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; the issuer of the securities has filed all Exchange&#160;Act reports and material required to be filed, as applicable, during the preceding twelve&#160;months (or such shorter period that the issuer was required to file such reports and materials), other than Form&#160;8 -K reports; and 
 &#8226; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; at least one year has elapsed from the time that the issuer filed current Form&#160;10 type information with the SEC reflecting its status as an entity that is not a shell company. 
 It is anticipated that following the consummation of the business combination, CCXI will no longer be a shell company, and as long as the conditions set forth in the exceptions listed above are satisfied, Rule&#160;144 will become available for the resale of CCXI&#8217;s restricted securities. 
 If the above conditions have been met and Rule&#160;144 is available, a person that has beneficially owned restricted CCXI Ordinary Shares for at least one year would be entitled to sell their securities pursuant to Rule&#160;144, provided that such person is not deemed to have been one of CCXI&#8217;s affiliates at the time of, or at any time during the three&#160;months preceding, a sale. If such persons are CCXI&#8217;s affiliates at the time of, or at any time during the three&#160;months preceding a sale, such persons would be subject to additional restrictions, by which such person would be entitled to sell within any three -month period only a number of securities that does not exceed the greater of: 
 &#8226; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; 1% of the total number of shares of common stock then outstanding; or 
 &#8226; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; the average weekly reported trading volume of the common stock during the four calendar&#160;weeks preceding the filing of a notice on Form&#160;144 with respect to the sale. 
 Sales by affiliates under Rule&#160;144, when available, will also be limited by manner of sale provisions and notice requirements. 
 As of the date of this proxy statement/prospectus, CCXI has &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; CCXI Ordinary Shares outstanding. Of these CCXI Ordinary Shares,&#160;&#160;&#160; &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; shares sold in the CCXI IPO are freely tradable without restriction or further registration under the Securities Act, except for any shares purchased by one of CCXI&#8217;s affiliates within the meaning of Rule&#160;144 under the Securities Act. All of the CCXI Ordinary Shares owned by the Sponsor are restricted securities under Rule&#160;144, in that they were issued in private transactions not involving a public offering. 
 It is expected that Rule&#160;144 will be available for the resale of the above -noted restricted securities as long as the conditions set forth in the exceptions listed above are satisfied following the Transactions, although these CCXI Ordinary Shares may be sold sooner to the extent they have been registered on a registration statement that has been declared effective by the SEC.

 Future Stockholder Proposals 
 Stockholder Proposals 
 The Proposed Bylaws establish an advance notice procedure for stockholders who wish to present a proposal before an annual meeting. To be properly brought before an annual meeting, business must be (i)&#160;specified in a notice of meeting given by or at the direction of the Board of Directors, (ii)&#160;otherwise brought before the meeting by or at the direction of the Board of Directors or the Chairman of the Board, or (iii)&#160;otherwise properly brought before the meeting by a stockholder who was a record owner of shares at the time of giving notice and at the time of the meeting, is entitled to vote at the meeting, and has complied with the notice procedures in the Proposed Bylaws, or who properly made such proposal in accordance with Rule&#160;14a -8 under the Exchange&#160;Act. Stockholders are not permitted to propose business to be brought before a special meeting. 
 To be timely, a stockholder&#8217;s notice must be delivered to the Corporation&#8217;s principal executive offices not less than 90&#160;days nor more than 120&#160;days prior to the one -year anniversary of the preceding year&#8217;s annual meeting. If the date of the annual meeting is more than 30&#160;days before or more than 60&#160;days after such anniversary date, notice must be delivered not more than the 120 th &#160;day prior to such annual meeting and not later than the 90 th &#160;day prior to such annual meeting or, if later, the 10 th &#160;day following the&#160;day on which public disclosure of the date of such meeting was first made. These notice requirements are expressly intended to apply to any business other than proposals made in accordance with Rule&#160;14a -8 under the Exchange&#160;Act and included in the Corporation&#8217;s proxy statement. 
 Stockholder Director Nominees 
 The Proposed Bylaws permit stockholders to nominate persons for election to the Board of Directors at an annual meeting or at a special meeting (but only if the election of directors is specified in the notice of meeting). To nominate a director, the stockholder must provide timely notice in writing and in proper form to the Secretary of the Corporation, provide the information required by the Proposed Bylaws with respect to each nominating person and nominee, and comply with all applicable requirements of the Exchange&#160;Act, including Rule&#160;14a -19 . The timing requirements for nominations at an annual meeting are the same as those described above under &#8220;Stockholder Proposals.&#8221; For special meeting nominations, notice must be delivered not earlier than the 120 th &#160;day nor later than the 90 th &#160;day prior to such special meeting or, if later, the 10 th &#160;day following the&#160;day on which public disclosure of the date of such meeting was first made. 
 The Proposed Bylaws provide that no nominating person shall solicit proxies in support of director nominees other than the Corporation&#8217;s nominees unless such person has complied with Rule&#160;14a -19 under the Exchange&#160;Act, and any failure to comply with Rule&#160;14a -19 will result in the disregard of such nominations.

 Enforceability of Civil Liability 
 CCXI is a Cayman Islands exempted company. If CCXI does not change its jurisdiction of incorporation from the Cayman Islands to Delaware by effecting the Domestication, you may have difficulty serving legal process within the United&#160;States upon CCXI.&#160;You may also have difficulty enforcing, both in and outside the United&#160;States, judgments you may obtain in U.S.&#160;courts against CCXI in any action, including actions based upon the civil liability provisions of U.S.&#160;federal or state securities laws. Furthermore, the courts of the Cayman Islands are unlikely (i)&#160;to recognize or enforce against CCXI, judgments of courts of the United&#160;States obtained against CCXI or CCXI&#8217;s directors or officers predicated upon the civil liability provisions of the securities laws of the United&#160;States or any state in the United&#160;States; and (ii)&#160;in original actions brought in the Cayman Islands, to impose liabilities against us or CCXI&#8217;s directors or officers predicated upon the civil liability provisions of the securities laws of the United&#160;States or any state in the United&#160;States, so far as the liabilities imposed by those provisions are penal in nature. In those circumstances, although there is currently no statutory enforcement or treaty between the United&#160;States and the Cayman Islands providing for enforcement of judgments obtained in the United&#160;States, the courts of the Cayman Islands will recognize and enforce a foreign money judgment of a foreign court of competent jurisdiction without retrial on the merits based on the principle that a judgment of a competent foreign court imposes upon the judgment debtor an obligation to pay the sum for which judgment has been given provided certain conditions are met. For a foreign judgment to be enforced in the Cayman Islands, such judgment must be final and conclusive, given by a court of competent jurisdiction (the courts of the Cayman Islands will apply the rules of Cayman Islands private international law to determine whether the foreign court is a court of competent jurisdiction), and must not be in respect of taxes or a fine or penalty, inconsistent with a Cayman Islands judgment in respect of the same matter, impeachable on the grounds of fraud or obtained in a manner, and/or be of a kind the enforcement of which is, contrary to natural justice or the public policy of the Cayman Islands. Furthermore, it is uncertain that Cayman Islands courts would enforce: (1)&#160;judgments of U.S.&#160;courts obtained in actions against us or other persons that are predicated upon the civil liability provisions of the U.S.&#160;federal securities laws; or (2)&#160;original actions brought against us or other persons predicated upon the Securities Act. Ogier has informed us that there is uncertainty with regard to Cayman Islands law relating to whether a judgment obtained from the U.S.&#160;courts under civil liability provisions of the securities laws will be determined by the courts of the Cayman Islands as penal or punitive in nature. A Cayman Islands Court may stay enforcement proceedings if concurrent proceedings are being brought elsewhere. However, CCXI may be served with process in the United&#160;States with respect to actions against CCXI arising out of or in connection with violation of U.S.&#160;federal securities laws relating to offers and sales of CCXI&#8217;s securities by serving CCXI&#8217;s U.S.&#160;agent irrevocably appointed for that purpose.

 We have audited the accompanying balance sheet of Churchill Capital Corp&#160;XI (the &#8220;Company&#8221;) as of December&#160;31, 2025, and the related statements of operations, changes in shareholders&#8217; deficit and cash flows for the period from June&#160;4, 2025 (inception) through December&#160;31, 2025, and the related notes (collectively referred to as the &#8220;financial statements&#8221;).  Basis for Opinion 
 These financial statements are the responsibility of the Company&#8217;s management. Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the Company&#8217;s financial statements based on our audit. We are a public accounting firm registered with the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United&#160;States) (the &#8220;PCAOB&#8221;) and are required to be independent with respect to the Company in accordance with the U.S.&#160;federal securities laws and the applicable rules and regulations of the Securities and Exchange Commission and the PCAOB.

The Company is not required to have, nor were we engaged to perform, an audit of its internal control over financial reporting. Accordingly, we express no such opinion. 
 Our audit included performing procedures to assess the risks of material misstatement of the financial statements, whether due to error or fraud, and performing procedures that respond to those risks.  CHURCHILL CAPITAL CORP&#160;XI 
 NOTES TO FINANCIAL STATEMENTS 
 DECEMBER 31, 2025 
 Note&#160;1 &#8212;&#160;Organization and Business Operations 
 Organization and General 
 Churchill Capital Corp&#160;XI (the &#8220;Company&#8221;) was incorporated as a Cayman Islands exempted company on June&#160;4, 2025 . The Company was incorporated for the purpose of effecting a merger, amalgamation, share exchange, asset acquisition, share purchase, reorganization or similar business combination with one or more businesses that the Company has not yet identified (the &#8220;Business Combination&#8221;). The Company is an &#8220;emerging growth company,&#8221; as defined in Section&#160;2(a)&#160;of the Securities Act&#160;of&#160;1933, as amended, or the &#8220;Securities Act&#8221;, as modified by the Jumpstart Our Business Startups Act&#160;of&#160;2012 (the &#8220;JOBS Act&#8221;). 
 As of December&#160;31, 2025, the Company had not yet commenced operations. All activity for the period from June&#160;4, 2025 (inception) through December&#160;31, 2025 relates to (i)&#160;the Company&#8217;s formation and the Initial Public Offering (as defined below), and (ii)&#160;subsequent to the Initial Public Offering, identifying a target company for an initial Business Combination., which is described below. The Company will not generate any operating revenues until after the completion of its initial Business Combination, at the earliest. The Company generates non -operating income in the form of interest income from the proceeds derived from the Initial Public Offering. The Company has selected December&#160;31 as its fiscal year end. 
 Sponsor and Initial Public Offering 
 The Company&#8217;s sponsor is Churchill Sponsor&#160;XI LLC (the &#8220;Sponsor&#8221;), an affiliate of M.&#160;Klien and Company, LLC.&#160;The Registration Statement on Form&#160;S -1 for the Initial Public Offering, initially filed with the U.S.&#160;Securities and Exchange Commission (the &#8220;SEC&#8221;) on November&#160;18, 2025 (File No.&#160;333 -291626 ), was declared effective on December&#160;16, 2025 (as amended, the &#8220;IPO Registration Statement&#8221;). On December&#160;18, 2025, the Company consummated the Initial Public Offering of 41,400,000 &#160;units at $ 10.00 per unit (the &#8220;Public Units&#8221;), which includes the full exercise of the underwriter&#8217;s Over -Allotment Option (as defined in Note&#160;7) in the amount of 5,400,000 &#160;units (the &#8220;Option Units&#8221;) at $ 10.00 per Option Unit (Note&#160;3), generating gross proceeds of $ 414,000,000 (the &#8220;Initial Public Offering&#8221;). Each Public Unit consists of one Class&#160;A Ordinary Share, par value $ 0.0001 per share, of the Company (the &#8220;Class&#160;A Ordinary Shares&#8221; and with respect to the Class&#160;A Ordinary Shares included in the Public Units, the &#8220;Public Shares&#8221;) and one -tenth of one redeemable warrant (each, a &#8220;Public Warrant&#8221;). Simultaneously, the Company consummated the sale of 500,000 &#160;units, (the &#8220;Private Placement Units&#8221;) (Note&#160;4), at a price of $ 10.00 per Private Placement Unit in a private placement to the Sponsor, generating gross proceeds of $ 5,000,000 (the &#8220;Private Placement&#8221;). Each Private Placement Unit consists of one Class&#160;A Ordinary Share and one -tenth of one redeemable warrant (the &#8220;Private Placement Warrants&#8221; and together with the Public Warrants, the &#8220;Warrants&#8221;). Each whole warrant entitles the holder to purchase one Class&#160;A Ordinary Share at a price of $ 11.50 , subject to adjustment. 
 Transaction costs amounted to $ 19,618,232 , consisting of $ 3,000,000 of cash underwriting fee (net of $ 3,210,000 underwriter&#8217;s reimbursement), $ 15,990,000 of Deferred Fee (as defined in Note&#160;6), and $ 628,232 of other offering costs. 
 The Trust Account 
 Following the closing of the Initial Public Offering on December&#160;18, 2025, an amount of $ 414,000,000 ($ 10.00 per Unit) from the net proceeds of the sale of the Units&#160;in the Initial Public Offering, and a portion of the proceeds of the sale of the Private Placement Units&#160;in the Private Placement, was placed in a Trust Account (the &#8220;Trust Account&#8221;). The proceeds held in the Trust Account are invested only in U.S.&#160;government treasury bills with a maturity of one hundred eighty -five ( 185 )&#160;days or less or in money market funds that meet certain conditions under Rule&#160;2a -7 under the Investment Company Act&#160;of&#160;1940 (the &#8220;Investment Company Act&#8221;) and that invest only in direct U.S.&#160;government obligations and, may at any time be held as cash or cash items, including in demand deposit accounts at a bank. Funds will remain in the Trust Account until the earlier of (i)&#160;the consummation of the initial Business Combination or (ii)&#160;the distribution of the Trust Account proceeds as described below. The remaining proceeds outside the Trust Account may be used to pay for business, legal and accounting due diligence on prospective acquisitions and continuing general and administrative expenses.

 Note&#160;1 &#8212;&#160;Organization and Business Operations (cont.) 
 The Company&#8217;s amended and restated memorandum and articles of association (the &#8220;Amended and Restated Articles&#8221;) provides that, other than the permitted withdrawals (as defined below), if any, none of the funds held in the Trust Account will be released until the earlier of (i)&#160;the completion of the initial Business Combination; (ii)&#160;the redemption of any Public Shares, that have been properly submitted in connection with a shareholder vote to approve an amendment to the Company&#8217;s Amended and Restated Articles (A)&#160;in a manner that would affect the substance or timing of its obligation to redeem 100 % of the Public Shares if it does not complete an initial Business Combination within 24&#160;months from the closing of the Initial Public Offering (or 27&#160;months from the closing of the Initial Public Offering if the Company has executed a letter of intent, agreement in principle or definitive agreement for an initial Business Combination within 24&#160;months from the closing of the Initial Public Offering) (the &#8220;Combination Period&#8221;) or (B)&#160;with respect to any other provision relating to the rights of holders of the Public Shares or pre -initial Business Combination activity; and (iii)&#160;the redemption of 100 % of the Public Shares if the Company is unable to complete an initial Business Combination within the Combination Period. The proceeds deposited in the Trust Account could become subject to the claims of the Company&#8217;s creditors, if any, which could have priority over the claims of the Company&#8217;s public shareholders. 
 Initial Business Combination 
 The Company&#8217;s management has broad discretion with respect to the specific application of the net proceeds of the Initial Public Offering, although substantially all of the net proceeds of the Initial Public Offering are intended to be generally applied toward consummating an initial Business Combination. The initial Business Combination must occur with one or more target businesses that together have an aggregate fair market value of at least 80 % of the assets held in the Trust Account (excluding the Deferred Fee (as defined below) and taxes payable on income earned on the Trust Account) at the time of the agreement to enter into the initial Business Combination. Furthermore, there is no assurance that the Company will be able to successfully effect an initial Business Combination. 
 The Company, after signing a definitive agreement for an initial Business Combination, will either (i)&#160;seek shareholder approval of the initial Business Combination at a meeting called for such purpose in connection with which shareholders may seek to redeem their shares, regardless of whether they vote for or against the initial Business Combination, for cash equal to their pro rata share of the aggregate amount then on deposit in the Trust Account as of two&#160;business&#160;days prior to the consummation of the initial Business Combination, including interest earned on the funds held in the trust account (net of amounts withdrawn to fund the working capital requirements, subject to an annual limit of $ 1,000,000 , and to pay taxes (&#8220; permitted withdrawals &#8221;)), (ii)&#160;provide shareholders with the opportunity to sell their Public Shares to the Company by means of a tender offer (and thereby avoid the need for a shareholder vote) for an amount in cash equal to their pro rata share of the aggregate amount then on deposit in the Trust Account as of two&#160;business&#160;days prior to the consummation of the initial Business Combination, including interest less permitted withdrawals. The decision as to whether the Company will seek shareholder approval of the initial Business Combination or will allow shareholders to sell their Public Shares in a tender offer will be made by the Company, solely in its discretion, and will be based on a variety of factors such as the timing of the transaction and whether the terms of the transaction would otherwise require the Company to seek shareholder approval, unless a vote is required by law or under Nasdaq rules. 
 Pursuant to the Company&#8217;s Amended and Restated Articles if the Company is unable to complete the initial Business Combination within the Combination Period, the Company will (i)&#160;cease all operations except for the purpose of winding up, (ii)&#160;as promptly as reasonably possible but no more than ten&#160;business&#160;days thereafter subject to lawfully available funds therefor, redeem the Public Shares, at a per -share price, payable in cash, equal to the aggregate amount then on deposit in the Trust Account including interest earned (which interest shall be net of permitted withdrawals and up to $ 100,000 of interest to pay dissolution expenses), divided by the number of then outstanding Public Shares, which redemption will completely extinguish the holders&#8217; rights as shareholders (including the right to receive further liquidating distributions, if any), subject to applicable law, and (iii)&#160;as promptly as reasonably possible following such redemption, subject to the approval of the Company&#8217;s remaining shareholders and the Company&#8217;s Board of Directors,

The Sponsor, officers and directors are not entitled to rights to liquidating distributions from the Trust Account with respect to any Founder Shares (as defined below) held by them if the Company fails to complete the initial Business Combination within the Combination Period.  Risks and Uncertainties 
 The Company&#8217;s ability to complete an initial Business Combination may be adversely affected by various factors, many of which are beyond the Company&#8217;s control. The Company&#8217;s ability to consummate an initial Business Combination could be impacted by, among other things, changes in laws or regulations, downturns in the financial markets or in economic conditions, inflation, fluctuations in interest rates, increases in tariffs, supply chain disruptions, declines in consumer confidence and spending, public health considerations, and geopolitical instability, such as the military conflicts in Ukraine, between the United&#160;States, Israel and Iran and other in the Middle East, and Southwest Asia or other armed hostilities. The Company cannot at this time predict the likelihood of one or more of the above events, their duration or magnitude or the extent to which they may negatively impact the Company&#8217;s ability to complete an initial Business Combination. 
 Liquidity and Capital Resources 
 As of December&#160;31, 2025, the Company had $ 736,204 of cash and a working capital surplus of $ 932,087 . In order to finance transaction costs in connection with its initial Business Combination, the Sponsor or an affiliate of the Sponsor, or the Company&#8217;s officers and directors may, but are not obligated to, loan the Company funds as may be required (&#8220;Working Capital Loans&#8221;). If the Company completes its initial Business Combination, the Company would repay the Working Capital Loans. In the event that the initial Business Combination does not close, the Company may use a portion of proceeds held outside the Trust Account to repay the Working Capital Loans but no proceeds held in the Trust Account would be used to repay the Working Capital Loans. If the Sponsor makes any Working Capital Loans, up to $ 1,500,000 of such loans may be convertible into units of the post business combination entity at a price of $ 10.00 per unit at the option of the lender. The units and the underlying securities would be identical to the Private Placement Units. As of December&#160;31, 2025, the Company had no borrowings under the Working Capital Loans. 
 Additionally, to fund working capital, the Company has permitted withdrawals available up to an annual limit of $ 1,000,000 . These permitted withdrawals are limited to only the interest available that has been earned in excess of the initial deposit at the Initial Public Offering. For the year ended December&#160;31, 2025, the Company did not withdraw any amounts from the Trust Account for working capital purposes. As of December&#160;31, 2025 the Company had $ 1,000,000 available for permitted withdrawals for the period from December&#160;18, 2025 until December&#160;18, 2026, which is the 1 -year anniversary of the Initial Public Offering.

 Note&#160;2&#160;&#8212;&#160;Summary of Significant Accounting Policies 
 Basis of Presentation 
 The accompanying financial statements are presented in U.S.&#160;dollars and have been prepared in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United&#160;States of America (&#8220;U.S.&#160;GAAP&#8221;) and pursuant to the accounting and disclosure rules and regulations of the Security and Exchange Commission (&#8220;SEC&#8221;). 
 Emerging Growth Company Status 
 As an &#8220;emerging growth company,&#8221; as defined in Section&#160;2(a)&#160;of the Securities Act, as modified by the JOBS Act, the Company may take advantage of certain exemptions from various reporting requirements that are applicable to other public companies that are not emerging growth companies including, but not limited to, not being required to comply with the auditor attestation requirements of Section&#160;404 of the Sarbanes -Oxley Act, as amended, reduced disclosure obligations regarding executive compensation in its periodic reports and proxy statements, and exemptions from the requirements of holding a non -binding advisory vote on executive compensation and shareholder approval of any golden parachute payments not previously approved. 
 Section&#160;102(b)(1)&#160;of the JOBS Act exempts emerging growth companies from being required to comply with new or revised financial accounting standards until private companies (that is, those that have not had a Securities Act registration statement declared effective or do not have a class of securities registered under the Securities Exchange&#160;Act&#160;of&#160;1934, as amended) are required to comply with the new or revised financial accounting standards. The JOBS Act provides that a company can elect to opt out of the extended transition period and comply with the requirements that apply to non -emerging growth companies but any such election to opt out is irrevocable. The Company has elected not to opt out of such extended transition period which means that when a standard is issued or revised and it has different application dates for public or private companies, the Company, as an emerging growth company, can adopt the new or revised standard at the time private companies adopt the new or revised standard. This may make comparison of the Company&#8217;s financial statement with another public company which is neither an emerging growth company nor an emerging growth company that has opted out of using the extended transition period difficult or impossible because of the potential differences in accounting standards used.
